The journal row says how many characters were stripped (extra.states_stripped). A request without a framed line is not touched, so with the flag off, and on the raw path, every byte is as before.

Outside the thinking (ui.states_channel, S1, 2026-10-02: the lines must be outside the thinking): reasoning keeps the placement above, and every profile stored before S1 keeps it; content, the seed profiles' value and so a new profile's, sends every line as a content delta of its own, never through the tool-call buffer or the <think> opener: before the reasoning starts, between two of its parts, after it. opencode (reasoning_content) shows them in its text part: the AI SDK ends the reasoning part at a content delta and opens a new one at the next reasoning delta, and all content of a response (its lines and its answer) lands in the one text part it opens at the first content delta, which sits above the reasoning parts. Sent back, opencode's reasoning parts are joined with nothing between them, so the reasoning is Qwen's exactly, and the content's lines are stripped like the reasoning's. In tags (and both, whose content is the tags text) a line said before the block opens goes out before <think>, one said after </think> after it, and one said while the block is open waits for its close and goes out right after </think>: outside it there is no place the client sends back as it was (Hermes keeps every block's reasoning, joined with a blank line, and the prompt would change); of the thinking lines only the newest waits. A non-streamed answer carries all its lines at the head of its content. tests/test_state_channel.py checks the stream, the strip on the checkpoint's template, and the replay through the handler (the same prompt ids, the same usage).

In time order in opencode (ui.states_channel: inline, X1, 2026-10-03). Screenshots of 09:23 and 10:03 (opencode 1.18.34, content): every line of a turn in one text block at its top, and in a turn that thought and then answered, the line and the whole answer above "Thought: 20.1s". Read in opencode's binary (its bundled @ai-sdk/openai-compatible, the module createOpenAICompatible comes from, and its SessionProcessor): the provider opens one text part per response at the first content delta (text-start, id txt-0) and never ends it before the stream does, so the answer is appended to the part the first line opened; a reasoning delta that follows a content delta or a tool_calls delta ends the open reasoning part and opens a new one (the processor makes a part with a fresh ascending id), and parts render in the order they were made. The TUI titles a reasoning part with its first line when that line is **title** and a blank line: + Thought: <title> · 1m 31s collapsed, Thinking: <title> while it streams. inline sends each line as a {"tool_calls": []} delta (the provider ends the open reasoning part on it; the list is empty, so no tool part) and a reasoning delta **› text** , never content: each line opens a reasoning part of its own, titled by it, at the moment it happens, Qwen's reasoning goes on in that part, and the answer's text part opens where the answer starts, after them. A line said after the answer began opens a part after the text part. The strip takes the title form out like the others (opencode sends the reasoning parts back joined with nothing between them), so the prompt ids are the ones without the lines. tags and both have no reasoning parts: there inline is content, byte for byte (Hermes). A non-streamed answer carries the lines at the head of its content, as content does. tests/test_state_inline.py checks the stream, the parts through a port of opencode's rules, the replay, Hermes, the waiting line, and runs opencode's own parser in node when the machine has node and an opencode binary (tools/opencode_bundle.py takes the provider module out of the binary, tools/opencode_parts.mjs feeds it a recorded stream): opencode 1.18.32 and 1.18.34 give the same parts.

Open WebUI's status line (0.3.51-test, SRV-237, SRV-249). Open WebUI 0.11.4 times a reasoning block from its first reasoning_content delta to its first content delta and shows that as "Thought for N seconds"; the waiting and reading lines went out as reasoning, so a summary with thinking off that read 12,874 tokens showed "Thought for 14 seconds" (its block held only the two reading lines), and a one-line answer that waited 35.8 s showed "Thought for 34 seconds". Open WebUI hands a stream chunk that carries an event key to its event emitter, and an event of type status is the line under the model's name that its tools and web search use, kept with the message. For the client kinds in QWEN38_STATUS_CLIENTS (default open-webui; empty: the profile's channel, as before) every line said before the model's first generated token (the router's and the packages' lines, the waiting and the reading lines) goes out as {"choices": [], "event": {"type": "status", "data": {"description": ..., "done": false}}}, and at the first token one last event, done, says what the wait was ("Read 12,874 tokens in 14 s", "Waited 31 s, then read …"). The reasoning block then opens with the model's own first piece, and a turn that does not think shows no "Thought for" at all. Lines after the first token keep the profile's channel. A refusal after a wait closes the status line before its error chunk.

The progress lines (queue, prefill, thinking; S1) are templates with numbers, no model: the narrator never writes them. ui.progress sets them: mode (on, also for a profile without the key; off), prefill_every_s (10), thinking_every_s (120) and thinking_every_tokens (4,096). They go only into a stream. The prefill's rate is the live view's (the first chunk left out, server/api/activity.py), so the first line comes after the second chunk, and a prefill with less than prefill_every_s left at that point says nothing. The thinking line counts from the first token. A request that has to wait for the engine opens its stream at its first waiting line, before it has the engine: what would have been a refusal after that (the queue's timeout, a prompt too long, the memory gate) ends the stream with an error object (its code, 429 for the queue) beside finish_reason: "error" and [DONE], and the ledger keeps the refusal's status. Before the engine is held nobody knows whether a tags answer opens a block, so in the reasoning channel a tags request shows no waiting line (reasoning_content and both show it as reasoning). The in-context stage's prefill (Qwen classifying inside the conversation) runs before the turn's stream starts and shows no progress line.

docs.title: The narrator writes the lines (ui.narrator, P1)
docs.text:
With a profile's ui.narrator: on beside ui.states: on (the Profiles screen, off by default and absent from every stored profile), each state line is written by a small model inside the engine instead of the template: the narrator role, MiniCPM5-2B (QWEN38_NARRATOR_MODEL=minicpm5-2b, the checkpoint under QWEN38_NARRATOR_DIR). It is a plain Llama-architecture decoder in PyTorch (engine/generative/llama.py), BF16, eager, greedy, with its own tokenizer and chat template (thinking off) and its own KV cache of 1,024 rows; its greedy text equals transformers' LlamaForCausalLM on the same weights (tools/narrator_reference.py). It gets the step's kind, what that kind means and its facts in words (the class's label and the effort, a cap, the tools and files of a check, the counts) and answers with one line; nothing of Qwen but text reaches it.

The limits: at most 14 words and 24 tokens, inside the role's latency_budget_ms (150 ms by default, the roles document), counted from the call to the last token; a request spends at most four budgets on its lines. A line the model cannot finish in time, at its token cap, with too many words or markup, or with an error, is the template (the journal row's extra.states[].narrator says why, with the milliseconds and the tokens). The model is not loaded at the start: the first narrated line starts its load through the residency planner (role narrator, a 6 GiB claim, never during a hold or beside a decision model's load) and is the template, as every line is until it is loaded. The roles document's narrator.mode says how it runs: on writes the lines, shadow keeps them in the journal only while the client sees the templates, off never asks it.

It runs on the request's own thread when the line goes out (before the prefill for the router's line, between two of Qwen's rounds for the monitor's, after the last token for the tool checks): Qwen waits meanwhile, nothing of Qwen runs beside it, and the engine's lock is held at most the budget and one step a line. Its weights and cache live in a memory pool of their own on a stream of their own, left out of the engine's ceiling like the decision models'. A narrated line goes out framed as " › <text>⁠ ": a WORD JOINER (U+2060, invisible and not whitespace) closes the text, so the strip takes a narrated line of any text, which no template matches, wherever it sits. GET /v1/conductor/narrator/status, POST /v1/conductor/narrator/load|unload and POST /v1/conductor/narrator/try ({events: [{kind, facts, extra?}], budget_ms?, max_tokens?}, the lines in the idle window) are its routes; tools/narrator_measure.py is the live check.

docs.title: The narrator sums up each thought (ui.narrator: thoughts, N2)
docs.text:
Asked on 2026-10-03: for each stretch of thinking, a line like "thought about 2 min about X and Y" in two short sentences, the small model reading only the thought. With a profile's ui.narrator: thoughts beside ui.states: on (off by default; the other lines stay templates) the narrator's model, Qwen3.5-0.8B (QWEN38_NARRATOR_MODEL=qwen3.5-0.8b, or qwen3.5-2b; the checkpoint under ~/.qwen38-spark-engine/models/<name> when QWEN38_NARRATOR_DIR is empty), writes one line per thought: "Thought 1m 43s: planned the level layout and decided on a fixed timestep; next it writes game.js". The model runs on the engine's own Qwen3.5 forward (engine/generative/qwen35.py: Qwen38Engine from the BF16 checkpoint, no new layer code, the vision and MTP tensors left out, the tied head), with a cache of its own (4,096 rows), its decode step from a CUDA graph captured at load (the graph-safe body Qwen's verify graphs use; a capture that fails leaves the eager step, the status says why), in the slot's memory pool and stream. Its tokenizer is the 27B's (the same vocabulary and merges, checked at load against the served checkpoint's tokenizer.json), so it reads Qwen's own ids of the thought, the last 1,500 of them, without a second tokenisation, after a fixed head (instructions and three made-up examples, 632 tokens, prefilled once per load and kept) and the answer begun with "It". Thinking off, greedy, at most 40 tokens; the line keeps two sentences, at most 45 words and 320 characters (clean_summary); the duration and the token count are the engine's.

When: a stretch of thinking that ends (the block closed by Qwen or by a hidden close, or the turn ending inside it) gets a thought line if it had at least 128 tokens; a long thinking's progress mark (ui.progress: every 2 minutes or 4,096 tokens) gets the summary of the thought since the last mark as its thinking line ("Thinking 4m 10s: …"), the template when a summary is still being written. Qwen waits while the narrator runs, so its time is rationed: in slices of at most the role's latency_budget_ms (150 ms), on the request's thread between two rounds, at most 3 % of the time since Qwen's first token over the request; what is left at the turn's end gets up to 500 ms more (the decode is over; the finish waits). A summary not done then, a refusal by the residency planner, an error or an answer the clean refuses: the template (thought 1 min, 4,096 tokens), and the line's narrator record says why. A long thought has earned its summary by the time it ends, so its line goes out right after it; a short one's goes out while Qwen writes the answer, or at the end. The lines are state lines in the profile's channel, framed with the sentinel and stripped from every prompt; never tokens, never in usage; the journal row keeps each as extra.states[] (the summary, the template, the milliseconds, slices, tokens, the window, why) and the request's totals as extra.narrator. The roles document's narrator.mode: shadow journals the line and shows the template, off never asks. tools/thought_narrator_measure.py is the GPU measurement (in a hold: 20 real thoughts' summaries, their latency, Qwen's decode with and without).

docs.title: The voice: live lines while Qwen works (ui.narrator: live, v3)
docs.text:
The requirement (2026-10-04): sentences of mixed length about what the model is doing right now. With a profile's ui.narrator: live beside ui.states: on (the coding and chat profiles from 0.3.28-test to 0.11.2; off by default since 0.11.3), the client gets one line of what Qwen is doing at the moment, in the profile's channel (opencode: the title of a reasoning part of its own, inline):

› code edit, maximum effort
› reading 20,745 tokens, about 18 s left
› thinking 25 s: designing a 140x15 tile map with pits, coins, enemies and platforms
› thinking 3 min: why the player's velocity is set to bounce after hitting an enemy
› thought 7 min: <what it decided>
› writing render.js: the vector art for the player and the enemies
› writing render.js, 211 lines so far

Facts come from the engine, never from a model: the timer, a tool's action and target (read from the open tool-call block as Qwen writes it), a write's line count, the queue's place, the prefill's tokens. The small model (the narrator role, a Qwen3.5 model on the engine's own forward, reading Qwen's own token ids) writes only the short phrase after them, from a window of what Qwen wrote last: what the thinking is about now (every every_s = 25 s from first_s = 15 s), what a thought of at least thought_min_s = 10 s decided (its own earlier lines and its last ~600 ids), what a write is for (the call and the body's first 700 characters), a plan in the answer. One fixed prompt head (instructions and ten made-up examples) serves every task and both languages, so the model keeps its state once per load and prefills only the window. Every phrase passes voice.clean: a file name or a number it holds must be in the text the model read, most of its content words too (English), no first person, no markup, no copy of an example, nothing like one of the last four lines. A phrase that fails is not said: a tool line is then the facts alone, a thinking line is skipped (the template "still thinking, 3 min so far (8,192 tokens)" comes after fallback_s = 120 s without any line).

Nothing for a short turn: no thinking line before 15 s, no thought line under 10 s, no tool line for a call done within tool_after_s = 1.5 s of its target being known (the client shows that call itself), and at most one model line per min_gap_s = 12 s. opencode's write writes content before filePath, so a write's path is known only at its end: its line says "writing a file" unless the body's first line names exactly one file that Qwen's words just before the call name too. The other lines (the router's, the packages', the queue's, the prefill's, the monitor's) go out in plain words (voice.natural), consecutive packages as one line, all in the user's language (German when the last user message reads German, voice.lang_of). Every line is framed with the narrator's sentinel, so the strip takes it out of whatever a client sends back: Qwen never reads one.

Qwen's time: the phrases are written in slices of at most 150 ms on the request's own thread between two of Qwen's rounds, the device synchronised first. A request's small-model time is one share (narrator.Share, ui.live.share = 3 % of the time since Qwen's first token); the voice draws on it first and the shadow reader's in-turn reading (shadow.Inline) gets what is left, at most its own 2 %, so the two together stay inside the decode gate. A phrase not done at the turn's end gets end_ms = 400 ms more. ui.live overrides any of the timings. The journal row keeps every line (extra.states[], with shown for a line said in words and for a phrase the model's task and window with its milliseconds and its reason) and the request's totals in extra.voice. The live view's request row carries the newest line (line), which the dashboard shows on the Live card and in the request's row.

Off by default since 0.11.3 (SRV-534): the roles document's narrator.mode is off and no shipped profile sets ui.narrator, so the model never loads and the residency plan holds no claim for it; POST /v1/conductor/narrator/load answers 409 role_off, and a box whose stored documents still had the old shipped values (live in coding and chat, the role on) gets off by a one-time migration unless a stored version had another value. With the role on, the model stays loaded: ops/start.sh asks POST /v1/conductor/narrator/load ({"service_start": true}) after the decision models, and a keeper thread in the server loads it again in an idle window whenever it is not loaded (a release, three failed calls, a refusal). Before 0.3.28 it loaded on its first line, copying its batches under the engine lock between the rounds of whatever turn was running: 734.5 s on 2026-10-04. Switch it off per profile with ui.narrator: thoughts (v2) or off, for every profile with the roles document's narrator.mode: off. tools/voice_replay.py replays a real opencode session through the voice's code (export from opencode's database, run with the model on the CPU or a GPU) and prints the lines a reader would have seen.

docs.title: Turn snapshots, turn outcomes and the cards (J1, 2026-10-02)
docs.text:
A profile's outcomes section (each switch off when absent, which is every profile stored before it) and the router document's optional outcomes section (the settings over the defaults in tandemapp/conductor/schema.py, OUTCOMES) drive the plan "Laya as the test judge, state snapshots, turn outcomes and the client protocol":

switch values what it does snapshots off, on the turn snapshot on the NVMe beside the transcript block mode off, shadow, act the Tier 0 outcome: journaled (shadow), or the effort and the note (act) cards off, shadow, on the client tool card and cards.harness kept live in the session's notes evaluate off, shadow, act E-b and E-c; with the router's outcomes.evaluate.ask.mode: shadow, Qwen asked in place on a narrowed case judge off, shadow Laya asked on the narrowed cases after the request, journaled only retrieve off, shadow, on a low-quality or stuck outcome retrieves the package that fits the work

The snapshot (tandemapp/conductor/outcomes.py) is built at the start of every request whose newest message is a tool result, before the router's effort, from the body alone: the calls since the last snapshot (a call is taken once, by its id; a session first seen mid-way counts only what came after its last user message), their results' heads and tails, the files written, the screenshots' hashes (of their base64, the same equality as the bytes') and sizes, a console read's levels, checker lines, exit codes, a test runner's counts, the tandem_state JSON a result carries and its diff, a scratch log's tail ({tandem_scratch}/*.log, or .tandem/*.log in a project from before 0.3.41-test). The transcript writer stores it as snapshots/turn-<n>.json beside block n, 0600, at most 32 KB (tails clipped first), the images under shots/ (the newest 5 a session; older snapshots keep the hash), and the block's runtime section gets one snapshot: line. It takes 0.023 ms a request (median, the two Mario sessions on the box CPU). Every string of the file passes the secret-pattern refusal first, as a transcript block does, and so do the outcomes' evidence lines and every digest a note carries.

The outcome is the first label of outcomes.order whose facts matched: no_visible_change (the same screenshot, the same output of an output tool, or the same state dump after a write), regression (a checker reading worse than the session's best, more failed tests than the same command had, a state key gone), error (a non-zero exit code, failed tests, an error-level console message, an error line in a run's output), low_quality (a failing reading at least low_quality.far of its limit away, or one gate failing low_quality.fails times in a row), surprise (a state number the router document names, e.g. lives <= 0; a test run of 0 tests; an empty write), stuck (no write and no better number for stuck.turns tool turns or stuck.minutes), tool_misuse (a tool that was not offered, a required argument missing, a call the client refused), test_faked (an evaluate script that assigns to a member of an object it did not declare: keys['ArrowRight'] = true, mario.x = flagX), environment (an OS error string: connection refused, address in use, no such file, permission denied, command not found), lost_context (the first calls after a compaction read none of the state files). progress when only progress facts matched, none when there was nothing to read. A read's text is never parsed for errors, and no fact is a word that decides what anybody meant. Every outcome is journaled (kind: outcome, task outcome) with its evidence, the effort and the note; the route row carries extra.outcome.

In act, outcomes.effort sets the turn's level (no visible change and regression xhigh, error high; never below the class's), held for raise_turns tool turns or until a progress; the labels in acting add their note from outcomes.notes once per signature (the E-a note carries the snapshot's digest, at most limits.digest_chars). A note is a router note: it goes in at the end of the last message and replays at the same token position on every later request, so the resident prefix holds; it is an act under the profile's caps (the monitor adopts it, Supervisor.adopt), and at a cap the effort still changes and the note is dropped (note.cap).

The cards: for a class in cards.classes with tools, the tool card (the request's own tools: names, required arguments starred, the path arguments; then the client kind's pitfalls package from cards.pitfalls) and cards.harness are notes kept live: each goes in while no live note carries it (the first turn, after a compaction) and replays after. A tool-misuse outcome brings the tool card back as its note.

Evaluation (step 6): E-c gives stuck and low quality evaluate.effort (xhigh) and the re-plan note with the digest; E-b hands the turn's digest to the claim check (E2), whose note carries it in act (shadow journals its size, detail.digest). Qwen in place (evaluate.ask.mode: shadow, off by default because it costs a prefill on every narrowed turn) asks the in-context stage's forward a failure | clean | unclear question on a run's output with no exit code and no counts, before the turn's prefill; the answer is journaled (task in_place) beside the twin and changes nothing.

The judge (step 7, tandemapp/conductor/judge.py): on the same narrowed cases (failure) and on a scratch log's tail (build), Laya is asked after the request on the judge's thread through the tester role with judge.deadline_ms (100), and every outcome, answered or not, is a row (task judge) beside the twin. The tester role is the judge's own (L1, 2026-10-03: until then the judge asked through the router's decider role, and with routing Qwen's since router v7 it wrote no row in 0.3.15's verification): endpoint self, model auto (the deciders document's questions.judge may name one), mode on; a roles document stored before it gets the built-in role. The digest is cut to what the model reads, its head and tail, before it is asked (laya-english reads 1,120 characters; the decider client used to keep the front). tools/judge_report.py reads them back: per question the coverage, the twin's agreement, the confident precision on the rows labelled right or wrong, and the gate (0.95 and 0.3) a question must pass before it may act.

Retrieval (step 8): a low-quality or stuck outcome asks the router's package question over retrieve.packages; the package that fits is the note (with E-c's re-plan note when evaluate is on), once per signature.

Two cards are kept live the same way on the coding classes with tools. The tool card lists the request's own tools (names, required arguments starred, which take a path) with the client's pitfalls package (tools-opencode, tools-hermes). The tandem-harness card says what the runtime around the model does and where its addresses are.

docs.title: The package library (R1, 2026-10-03)
docs.text:
Asked on 2026-10-03: many packages on many subjects, so the model can search and use them later. 44 skills were written (opencode's SKILL.md: frontmatter name and description, the text that goes in, then ## Reference with snippets and commands) and an INDEX.md whose table names the classes each fits. On the box they are ~/.qwen38-spark-engine/conductor/skills/library/<name>/SKILL.md, and each is a package with library: true, source skill:<name> (the library directory is in skill_dirs), max_tokens 500 (the server cuts at 3.5 characters a token; no body is cut). A library package's text is its part before ## Reference; the reference is read only through the route below. tools/library_install.py copies the files, registers the packages and sets a profile's switch (dry run by default; --measure counts on the engine's tokenizer).

The index (tandemapp/conductor/libsearch.py): BM25 (k1 1.2, b 0.75) over every enabled library package's name (three times), description (twice) and text; words are lower-case letters and digits, a plural s dropped, a few function words left out, each query word counted once. It is rebuilt when the packages version, a SKILL.md or INDEX.md moves or a file comes or goes, looked at once a second at most: 44 skills build in about 2 ms and a 900-character query searches in about 40 µs on the box CPU. No embeddings.

Retrieval by the router, a profile's library switch (off, absent included: nothing runs and the index is never built; shadow; on; a profile in shadow lowers on to shadow). On a new user message (not a tool turn, not a compaction), and on a tool turn whose J1 outcome is listed in the router's library.outcomes (low quality and stuck), the digest of the user's message (and the outcome's reasons and file types) is searched; INDEX.md's classes keep the skills that fit the turn's class (class_filter; a skill INDEX.md does not list stays in; chat fits none). The best candidates (4) go to the router's package question (packages.fit, question id packages: the decider or Qwen picks a description or none, at accept 0.6), up to max_picks (1; at 2 the second is asked without the first). With on each pick is a note at the prompt's tail after the class's block, the cards and the outcome's note, under header ("A skill from the TandemLLM library fits this task: {name}. …"), replayed at its position on every later turn; a skill live in the session is not offered again, and an outcome's pick counts as an act under the caps. The card package (tandem-library, 191 tokens: the library exists, how to search it and read a skill with curl) is kept live on the card_classes with tools, like cards.harness. With shadow the row's extra.library (the trigger, the query's size, the candidates and their scores, the picks, how, the times) and shadow.library / shadow.library_card say what would have gone in, and the prompt is the one off serves. A pick is asked once per message (or outcome signature) and session; with QWEN38_LIBRARY_HOLD=class (VIS-119; message, the default, asks on every new user message), on a class whose package answer holds for the class (package_sticky: class, the prose classes), once per class and session: a later message the class question keeps in that class takes the class's answer, picks and none alike (extra.library.held: class), and a live skill is not added twice. A shadow question that would go to Qwen through the server's own port first (the decider stage off, as on the shipped router; with --backends the proxy's stage override leaves the server's own requests there, a backend it relays to asks in place) is not asked before the queue (VIS-119, QWEN38_SHADOW_ASK, idle): on an idle box a Chat-tab message queued 1.41 s, 1.32 s of it that question, whose answer the request never reads (2026-10-31; the 26 answers in the box's last 500 rows were all none). The row says how: deferred; after the request ends, tandemapp/conductor/deferred.py's thread asks it once the server has been idle for QWEN38_SHADOW_ASK_IDLE_S seconds (5; nothing running, queued or in the router, the engine lock free), one question at a time, and the answer goes into the session's picks and, as an update of the request's row, into extra.library (with deferred.waited_ms) and shadow.library; a question that finds no idle moment within 600 s, or 16 already waiting, is dropped (deferred.dropped), and so is one whose turn ended in tool calls (tool_calls: the client's next step follows at once; an agent client's answer to a new message mostly starts with tool calls, so its shadow library rows mostly say dropped) or whose question failed (failed); a job whose message an earlier job already answered (a regenerate inside the idle time) takes that answer (cached) and asks nothing; a turn that failed open (SRV-763) asks none. inline asks before the queue as before, off asks nothing (how: shadow_off); on, a decider asked first, a plan under the engine lock and the test box ask in place. Asking the questions at once instead would not hide their time: the GPU serves their prefills one after the other (two class questions at once 1.32-1.44 s against 0.67-0.69 s alone; the class and the package question together 2.84-2.96 s against 3.0-3.4 s one after the other, the class answer then at 2.84 s; 2026-11-01). A plan decided under the engine lock (the in-context stage) asks the decider stages only and journals locked when there is none: Qwen through the server's own port would wait for the lock that plan holds (the class's own package question has that problem today: an 8 s qwen_timeout on 2026-10-02 at 14:22).

Search by the model (tandemapp/library_api.py): GET /v1/library/search?q=<words>&k=5&class=<id> answers [{name, description, score}], best first (k 1 to 20, q at most 1,000 characters, [] when no word matches); GET /v1/library/{name} answers {name, description, classes, body, reference}; GET /v1/library lists every enabled skill and the two routes. Open as the chat API and the Laya route (no key at the engine; a bearer is ignored), Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, OpenAI-shaped errors (422 invalid_request_error, 404 not_found for an unknown or disabled skill or no library, 429 rate_limited over 240 calls a minute with Retry-After). Every call is a journal row (kind: library_api, task list, search or read): the query as a hash and a length, never its text, k, the class, the names answered, the status, the time. The dashboard's Packages screen searches the library through this route; a profile's switch is on the Profiles screen and on the Packages screen's Library tab.

From a shell, with the session's address in $TANDEM_URL:

curl -s "$TANDEM_URL/v1/library/search?q=playwright+screenshot+test&k=5"
curl -s "$TANDEM_URL/v1/library/test-web"       # body and reference

docs.title: The Packages and Skills screen's reads (G2, 2026-10-03)
docs.text:
tandemapp/conductor/catalog.py, under the dashboard's read rule like every GET /v1/conductor/* (the tokens POST too: it writes nothing). Nothing here is on a request's path, nothing journals, and nothing changes what the router injects; the edits are the packages, router and profile documents' own versioned PUTs.

  • GET /v1/conductor/packages/catalog: every package of the packages document with its category (library; card: cards.harness, a client's pitfalls card, the library card; test_skill: one of the router's outcomes.retrieve.packages; task_skill: any other skill; package), its source and path, whether its text is there, the tokens of the text that goes in (Library.text with the package switched on) and of the whole text before the server's cut and of a library skill's reference, on the engine's tokenizer (tokenizer: engine; each text counted once, by its hash; without a tokenizer 3.5 characters a token, estimate), its limit (a library skill 350 tokens and the library card 200, the house rule tools/library_install.py checks; every other package its max_tokens) and whether the whole text is over it, the router classes and each profile's routing that list it, INDEX.md's class fit, and each profile's library switch.
  • GET /v1/conductor/packages/item/{name}: one package's frontmatter (parsed and as written), the body after it, a library skill's reference, the text that goes in, the tokens of each, and for a library skill its six nearest skills by the library's own BM25 (its name and description with its text as the query, itself left out); 404 for an unknown name.
  • POST /v1/conductor/packages/tokens {texts}: the tokens of 1 to 20 texts of at most 200,000 characters each, in order (the editor's counter); 400 otherwise.
  • GET /v1/conductor/packages/usage?name=&limit=: the journal's router rows of the last 7 days, per package the times it went in (a note part: the class's package, a library skill, the library card, a card by the row's client, an outcome's retrieved package), the times it would have (shadow notes and cards, an outcome note not applied) and the library's picks (extra.library.chosen, shadow or on), each for the last 24 hours and the week; with name, its newest limit rows (1 to 200, default 20; each with its session and class, its profile and its time); and the library's newest 50 retrieval rows (the candidates and their scores, the pick, how, applied) with the week's searches, picks and most picked skills.

The contract is four schemas under contracts/conductor-v1/: packages-catalog with packages-item, and packages-tokens with packages-usage.

docs.title: Laya for the model's scripts (/v1/laya/ask, L1, 2026-10-03)
docs.text:
The aim: the model reaches Laya through our provider, from the scripts it writes, to test any software. POST /v1/laya/ask (tandemapp/laya_api.py) is the small, stable shape a script needs, open like the chat API beside it (no key at the engine; the service is LAN-only behind the reverse proxy; a bearer a script sends is ignored): {question, choices | scale | neither, text | texts, threshold?, model?, deadline_ms?}. choices is a list of labels or {label: meaning} (2 to the model's 20); scale a list of 2 to 10 levels, lowest first; neither makes question a yes-no question. One text answers {label, p, sure, probs, model, ms, chars, read_chars, clipped} (a scale adds level and score, a yes-no yes); texts (at most api.max_texts, 16) answers {answers: [...], model, ms}, one forward a text. p is the label's probability and sure is p >= threshold (the document's 0.8 by default). Laya reads a window of its context less its question budget, 1,120 characters for laya-english: a longer text is cut by code to its head (a quarter) and its tail around [...], and the answer says so. It runs in the idle window, which is where a script runs, between two requests of its session; a caller that meets a running completion waits up to deadline_ms (15 s, at most 60 s), then gets 503 busy with Retry-After. Errors have the OpenAI shape, {error: {message, type, param?}}: 422 invalid_request_error (before any model runs), 429 rate_limited (api.rate_per_min, 240 texts a minute over every caller), 503 busy/loading/refused, 404 when off. The answers carry Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and OPTIONS answers the preflight, so a test inside the page the model builds (the browser tool's evaluate script) can fetch it. GET /v1/laya prints the contract and the limits. The deciders document's api section (mode, rate_per_min, max_texts, max_chars, deadline_ms, threshold; absent: the defaults, on) and questions.laya_api (the model, auto) configure it, on the Deciders screen's "Laya for scripts" panel, which also shows the calls since the start. Every call is a journal row (kind: laya_api, task ask): the type, the labels, the number of texts and their sizes, what was cut, the answers' labels and probabilities, the model, the time, the client kind; the question as a hash and a length, never a text. The contract is laya-ask and laya-ask-texts. The packages laya-testing (general on the coding classes: what Laya is, the call, and that the model must ask it about its evidence before "done") and laya-scripts (general on code_edit and debug: the helper {tandem_scratch}/laya.py and recipes for seven kinds of work: logs, CLIs, APIs, pages, games, data, regressions) teach it; the five kind skills carry one Laya example each. Since 0.3.41-test (SRV-163) the helper and the curl example name the provider only as {tandem_url} (a package text that calls /v1/laya, /v1/library or /v1/memory at a literal address is refused at save), the helper exits 3 with one line when the call fails ("the call failed on this machine, your code is not the cause") and laya-testing tells the model to go on without the verdict instead of debugging the transport: on the Spark, whose trust store lacks the LAN's private root CA, the saved packages' literal https:// address had cost a session up to 42 % of its time in certificate debugging.

The engine can serve small decision models itself (engine/decision/): models that answer typed questions over a text in one forward pass with calibrated probabilities. A question is a choice (one of N options), a score (an expected level) or a yes-no probability. Laya's three published checkpoints (Apache-2.0) are the models it serves: laya-english (ModernBERT-large, 512 tokens of state and question), laya-multilingual and laya-typed-decisions (1,024 tokens each). QWEN38_DECIDER_MODELS names the ones a server loads; empty, nothing of it is imported and its routes are absent.

POST /v1/laya/ask
{"question": "Does this test log show a failure?",
 "choices": {"failure": "a test failed or crashed", "clean": "every test passed"},
 "text": "<the tail of the log>"}
-> {"label": "failure", "p": 0.97, "sure": true, "probs": {...}, "model": "laya-english", "ms": 31}

The packages that teach it name the engine only as {tandem_url}; a package whose text calls /v1/laya, /v1/library or /v1/memory at a literal address is refused at save, because a literal https:// address fails wherever the machine running the model's scripts does not trust the server's certificate authority. The helper they give the model exits 3 with one line when the call fails (“the call failed on this machine, your code is not the cause”), and the model goes on without the verdict. The same packages keep their scratch files in {tandem_scratch}, have the model remove its state hooks (tandem_state, /__state, --dump-state) before it reports done unless the user asked for one, and forbid downloading a runtime or an executable. tools/packages_migrate.py applies these texts to a box's saved packages document as a new version.

docs.title: Laya plays the build (driver sessions and the playtest kit, X1, 2026-10-03)
docs.text:
Laya's intended use: it plays the software under test while Qwen writes it. The kit (tandemapp/laya_kit/, served as text at GET /v1/laya/kit/laya_drive.py and /v1/laya/kit/laya-drive.js, which the model copies into the session's scratch directory {tandem_scratch}) reads the program's state each step (a page's window.tandem_state(), a headless program's JSON line, a state command's output), asks POST /v1/laya/ask which action of a fixed set comes next (choices with meanings; a UI's state may list its own controls), applies it as input and logs the step to drive-log.jsonl beside the kit; a lost life, a game over, a win, a stuck spot (the same place for 20 steps) and the step budget are events. laya_drive.py browser starts a headless Chrome (or attaches with --cdp) and presses real keys and clicks over the DevTools protocol, stdlib only (Linux without user namespaces gets --no-sandbox, as Playwright starts Chromium there); proc drives a program over JSON lines, cmd a state command and an action command (CLIs, APIs with curl); laya-drive.js runs the loop inside the page with synthetic keys when only the browser tool reaches it, its log through laya_drive.py serve-log. laya_drive.py page URL --step ... is the check of a page without Laya playing it (0.3.45-test, SRV-195): the same headless Chrome loads the page, runs the steps with real input (click:SELECTOR or click:text=Label, key:Space*300, type:SELECTOR=text, wait:MS, read:JS, expect:JS, shot:NAME; a step that cannot run ends the script), takes screenshots at 1280 and 390 px (--widths) with a horizontal-overflow reading, collects console errors, uncaught exceptions and failed loads (one line each however often the page loads), reads window.tandem_state() when the page has it, asks Laya "Does this page check show a failure?" once (--no-laya), closes Chrome on every path and prints one JSON report with a PASS or FAIL verdict (exit 0, 1; 2 when no Chrome is found or the check itself fails, with the words "do not build another driver"); --timeout (90 s) bounds it. About 5 s for a one-file page. Chrome starts with --password-store=basic --use-mock-keychain in every mode: without them it waited about 25 s for the desktop keyring at its first network request. laya_drive.py report prints the run for Qwen: the outcomes, Laya's p50/p95 and unsure steps, the actions' mix, each death with its place (the last decision's), its cause and the decisions before it, deaths by place, stuck spots, the step budget.

A call with session is a driver step: its own rate, api.drive_rate_per_s (10) texts a second, not the scripts' minute; at most api.drive_sessions (4) live, api.drive_max_texts (36,000) each; 429 with Retry-After past any of them. No journal row a call: one laya_drive row a session when POST /v1/laya/drive/end {session, summary?} ends it (the kit always does) or api.drive_idle_s (30 s) after its last call, written at the next call of the routes: calls, texts, errors by kind, the labels' counts, p mean and lowest, unsure, ms p50/p95/max, seconds, how it ended, the question as a hash, and the driver's summary (episodes, steps, deaths, wins, timeouts, stuck, busy, fallbacks: numbers only). Latency: the server's path is 3.1 ms p50, 3.6 ms p95 (box CPU, fake model, 200 steps through HTTP, the batcher's 2 ms collation included); laya-english's forward on the box was 18.7 to 48.7 ms for one text in the journal of 2026-10-03, so a step is about 25 to 50 ms and 10 a second fit. The idle rule holds: the driver runs inside a tool call and opencode sends its next request when the tool returns. Of the 16 laya_api calls of 2026-10-03 against the requests timeline, 14 met an idle engine and 2 came while the request that wrote the tool call was finishing (opencode starts a tool once its call is complete in the stream; 96 and 115 ms before that request ended) and waited for it (148.5 and 187.8 ms); another client's request makes a step wait up to its deadline (two ticks in a real-time run), and the kit then applies its fallback action and logs busy. The package laya-playtest (294 tokens before its reference, an inline general library package: the core goes into the prompt, the recipes are GET /v1/library/laya-playtest) says when and how, and that every interactive build is playtested before "done"; laya-testing and test-web point at it. tools/playtest_install.py stores it, attaches it after laya-testing, and sets a profile's ui.states_channel: inline.

The same kit checks a page without Laya playing it: laya_drive.py page URL --step ... starts the kit's headless Chrome, runs the steps with real input (click:, key:, type:, wait:, read:, expect:, shot:), takes screenshots at 1280 and 390 px with an overflow reading, lists console errors, uncaught exceptions and failed loads, asks Laya once for a verdict, closes Chrome on every path and prints one report, in about 5 s. The testing packages make it the browser for a page: never a driver of the model's own, one check with every main control, fix, check again, then the final message, and no Laya playtest for a one-screen tool. The final message is for the user: what was built, where it is and how to open it, how to use it, one plain sentence on how it was checked, what is untested. Laya's labels and probabilities, the kit, state hooks, the scratch folder, draw calls and fps stay out of it, and a readout added only for the check is removed before “done” or kept behind ?debug. An opencode run that built a one-file page found no Chrome on its PATH, only Firefox, and spent the rest of its 600 s on a Marionette driver of its own; with the page check, five runs of the same task ended with a checked page and a report in 221 to 260 s (measured). The kit starts Chrome with --password-store=basic and --use-mock-keychain: without them every start waited about 25 s for the desktop keyring.

docs.title: The conductor's session monitor
docs.text:
--conductor raw|shadow|on switches the session monitor (tandemapp/conductor/monitor/). raw, the default, runs none of it: the output is the raw engine's, and there is no stall close either (a client's own max_reasoning_tokens still closes the block with the streamed phrase). shadow runs every rule and journals what it would do, and executes nothing. on executes, each task in the mode its policy gives it. off is accepted for raw. A request's X-Tandem: raw|shadow|on header can lower the server's mode, never raise it, and every completion response carries X-Tandem with the mode the request ran in. A request with n > 1 never acts (at most shadow).

The policy is a file, --conductor-policy (default ops/supervisor.yaml): every task's mode (off, shadow, act), every threshold and every text. It is validated at start against ops/supervisor.schema.json (JSON Schema, draft 2020-12), which python tools/conductor_policy.py --schema writes from the rule registry; python tools/conductor_policy.py [file] checks a file.

The monitor acts only at four safe points, from a fixed action set:

safe point when actions SP4 (the notes' SP0) the prompt is rendered, before prefill PROMPT_TAIL_NOTE, SET_THINK_BUDGET SP1 a verify block is committed and yielded CLOSE_REASONING, GIVE_UP SP2 the model wrote its end token, before it reaches the client CONTINUE_HIDDEN, GIVE_UP SP3 the answer ended (SP2's moment) and its calls are held REPAIR_CALL, REGENERATE_CALL, GIVE_UP

PASS is "nothing"; NOTIFY is out of band: the stall watchdog's watch sends it (below), never a request. What the client sees: a hidden close forwards the policy's phrase through the engine and streams only from the closer on (</think> in tags, nothing in reasoning_content); a hidden continue drops the end token and forwards the close phrase (inside the reasoning) or a hidden user turn with a nudge and an empty closed reasoning block (after it), and the answer follows in the same response; GIVE_UP is one visible sentence from the policy with finish stop. Caps: acts_per_request and acts_per_session_hour, and never the same hidden action twice in a row on one turn; beyond them an act becomes GIVE_UP. Tool calls are held only while a tool-call task can act (and never for a constrained request, tool_choice required or named: the grammar writes those calls).

A call written inside the reasoning (0.3.46-test, SRV-199): a turn of a request with tools that ends with complete <tool_call> blocks inside its reasoning, with nothing but whitespace (and the closer) after them and no answer, used to finish stop with no call and no text, because the parser reads the answer only (an Open WebUI agent chat stopped after "Let me see the full report"). E1 now has a case C: when every such block parses and names a tool the request offers, SP2 forwards the closer (the newline before it hidden, nothing when the block was already closed) and then the model's own call tokens as the answer, so the client receives the calls the model wrote, through the same parser and checks as any other, with no generation in between; the model then writes its end token. A block that does not parse or names another tool is case A or B as before, and two failed tries end in GIVE_UP's visible sentence, never a silent stop. E1 acts in the chat (Open WebUI) and general profiles too; a box whose stored profiles predate this sets E1 to act on the Monitor screen. On the reference box's ledger, 7 days before the change: 1 such stop in 322 Open WebUI rounds.

docs.title: Tool-call checks (SRV-113)
docs.text:
With a tool-call task able to act, every call of an answer is held until the answer ends; a block that does not parse is held too, not let out as content. At the end token every call is checked by every SP3 task, before any is released:

task rule what it decides wave 1 C4 malformed_call a block that does not parse: a deterministic fix (REPAIR_CALL: JSON with trailing commas or Python literals, an unquoted name=, a </parameter> that never came) or a hidden reminder with the parser's reason (REGENERATE_CALL, at most regenerations a request, then the block goes out as content as without the checks); the arguments against the tool's JSON schema (required keys, types); a call the token limit cut (GIVE_UP, never half a call) act; the schema check in shadow C3 repeated_call the same name and canonical arguments as the previous repeats - 1 calls of the current user turn, whose results (from the request's tool messages) were identical, none of them a wait (wait_s): "do something different" act C5 sequential_mutations two or more calls to tools that change something outside the conversation (kinds: send, schedule, create, write, delete): "one action at a time: the first, its result, then the next" (REGENERATE_CALL, at most regenerations (1) a request) shadow; act in tools C1 risk_floor the floors, a list in the policy: rm -rf outside the project root, git push, a write outside the root, a download piped into a shell; the root is the working directory opencode states in its system prompt shadow C2 project_rules what text alone can decide of AGENTS.md (only when the system prompt carries it): a numbered copy of a file the session used, a path under /tmp/, a written file over 400 lines; a call whose every path is on allow_paths is exempt from all three (default /tmp/opencode, opencode's own scratch; a path covers everything under it, * ? [ make a glob, ~ is home, a relative entry is under the project root) shadow

If all pass, the calls go out whole, each in one delta with an id made at release and indexes contiguous from 0. If any act fails, none goes out: the end token is dropped, a hidden turn shaped as the calls' tool result (templates.regen_turn) carries the reminders, and the model writes the set again in the same response; the client receives only the new calls, at index 0 again. An answer that ended without its end token (the token limit, a stop string) cannot be written again, so there a failure gives up. A block the client's own stop string cut is not a failure: C4 lets it out as the text it was (cut_by_stop), as the raw engine answers; only a block the token limit cut follows C4's cut (give_up). A profile turns each check's pack on or off (toolgate.risk, project, same_call, malformed, sequence) and sets its mode and thresholds. With the monitor raw, or no tool-call task able to act, calls stream as they always did. When the generation ends inside a block that streamed live (the token limit, the deadline, an end token inside a value), the block's text is not sent again as content: the client keeps the calls the stream closed and the open call as it was sent, with arguments that never close (until 0.3.31 the text went out a second time, and the next prompt carried it twice). A streamed request with stop strings is the one exception, with or without the monitor: its calls go out whole when their block closes, because a stop string can end the generation inside a block, and arguments already streamed cannot be taken back; such a cut block is the text it was, as in the non-streamed answer.

C3 in detail (SRV-473). A repeat is the call that would be the repeats-th (3) in a row with the same tool and canonical arguments (key order and whitespace do not count), after repeats - 1 results with the same content. Only the calls after the last user message count: a user message starts over. A run whose result came back after the client took wait_s (10 s) or more, from the end of the answer that issued it to the request that carried the result, is a wait (a poll of a running job) and breaks the streak (the session monitor keeps that time per call id). A test run again after an edit, or a file read after a write, has another call in between and passes. C3 can only fire on a request whose turn already ends with the streak, so it holds calls only there: with C3 the only tool-call task that acts, every other request streams its calls live, as with the pack off. Past the caps a finding gives up: no call goes out and the turn ends with texts.give_up. The shipped coding, chat-app, hermes, overnight and chat profiles have toolgate.same_call: true (chat's C3 acts too); general has it off. A box's stored profiles get it once at the next start (migration 2026-10-14-<name>-loop-guard), unless a stored version of the profile ever had it on: then the current value stays.

C5 in detail (SRV-623, policy 8). A call counts as a mutation when its tool's declaration says so (signals.tool_effects, the way SRV-243's tool_caps reads it; the messages are never read): send is a recipient parameter (to, recipient, channel, chat_id, ...) with a message parameter (body, message, text, content); schedule a time parameter (date, datetime, start, due, ...) with a subject (title, summary, subject, message, text); write a path with a body (SRV-243's write); create and delete the operation the tool's name opens with (after an MCP server prefix; its description's first word when the name states none: create, add, set, update, ... and delete, remove, cancel, ...). A name that opens with a read verb (get, list, search, read, fetch, ...) is a read whatever its parameters, as is an annotations.readOnlyHint of true; destructiveHint true is a delete. A shell is none: opencode reads through bash, often several calls at once. tool-eval-bench's send_email, create_calendar_event and set_reminder are mutations; its other nine tools, opencode's read, glob, grep, bash and webfetch, and Open WebUI's search_web and fetch_url are not; opencode's write and edit are writes. The check decides once an answer, at its second mutating call: two reads (TC-27), or a read beside one mutation, pass. The regeneration is C4's (templates.regen_turn); the client receives only the new calls. Its finding is about order, not a call that cannot run, so past regenerations, past the request's or the session's caps, and on an answer without its end token the calls go out as they are, journaled (fallback(regenerations=1), released(<cap>), ended(mutations=N)), never a give-up. C5 holds calls only on a request that offers a mutating tool. A constrained request (tool_choice required or named, or SRV-619's calls-or-document grammar for response_format with tools) holds nothing and journals C5 in shadow, as every SP3 act. Shipped: tools acts; coding, chat-app, hermes and chat journal it (toolgate.sequence: true, the task in shadow); general and overnight have it off. A box's stored profiles get it once at the next start (migration 2026-10-19-<name>-c5) when they have neither the task nor the pack; a stored monitor document gets the task with tools/monitor_migrate.py --put http://127.0.0.1:8000 --tasks C5.

SP4's splices touch the prompt's tail only, so the resident prefix and the state store stay valid: a note goes into the last message just before its turn end (the template refuses a system message that is not first), and thinking off replaces the generation prompt's open <think>\n with the closed empty block the template writes for enable_thinking: false. Neither changes the system turn or reasoning_effort, which render as the prompt's first tokens.

Hidden tokens are excluded from usage's counts in the default client mode (completion_tokens counts streamed tokens, prompt_tokens what the client sent; the prompt's hidden tokens are prompt_tokens_details.hidden_tokens, see Streaming). Engine usage mode includes hidden prompt tokens in the occupied context count; hidden output tokens remain excluded from completion_tokens. Hidden tokens are never in the suffix store, and a response the monitor acted on is not stored in the response cache. The KV holds them, and until 0.3.14-test every turn re-read the previous turn's whole output: the resident prefix anchored prefill chunks only, and the session snapshot that would hold the state after the generation is over the store's entry cap for any long session. From 0.3.14-test the resident prefix keeps an end anchor at the end of every generation (--end-anchor, on), and the hidden tokens are put back into the next prompt where the rows hold them (after the router's notes, before SP4), when the prompt then starts with every token up to that anchor; the turn forwards only its new messages (caches.md). Put back, they stay hidden: excluded from client-mode prompt_tokens, the suffix store and the response cache; the journal row has extra.end_replayed.

Sessions: the conversation id the client sends (conversation_id, session_id or user in the body, X-Conversation-Id, opencode's x-session-id); else a compaction request (no tools, one user message) joins the most recent session and the next unseen prefix joins it too; else a hash of the first lineage_tokens prompt tokens, joined within join_window_s. The state is an LRU of max_sessions, with tool calls and results as hashes, never text.

Every decision is one journal event and one [conductor] log line (task, decision, reason, counts; never a text).

docs.title: The claim check (E2, 2026-10-02)
docs.text:
In three Mario sessions on 2026-10-02 Qwen ended with "Done … verified in-browser" after a test that set keys['ArrowRight'] = true instead of pressing a key, read "lost all 3 lives in 1.5 s" as "the damage system works", and teleported Mario to the flag to test the win. E2 (claim_check, tandemapp/conductor/monitor/claimcheck.py) checks such a claim before the end token reaches the client. The trigger is structural: the turn's class (the router's, RequestEvent.cls) is in classes (code_edit, debug, design_ui, three_d, drawing), the request offered tools, the model wrote its end token after a non-empty answer with no tool call (an empty one is E1's), and the session has a write behind it (a write_tools call in the request's history, or one the monitor recorded). Once a request; after per_session (2) notes on one session the event is claim_check_exhausted and the message goes out as written. No word of the answer decides anything structural.

Then Qwen itself answers, thinking off, one letter a question: Q1 (claim_question), does the message tell the user the work is finished, working or verified (claim at claim_at, 0.85, or above); on a claim, Q2 (evidence_question, {since} the tools called since the last write), what the tool evidence since the last write says: supported, no_run_after_last_write, errors_in_evidence, surprise_unexplained or test_faked (taken at admit_at, 0.6). The router's Qwen stage cannot be used: it calls the server's own port, and at SP2 the request holds the engine lock, so the call would wait for its own lock until it timed out. The questions are asked in place instead, as the in-context stage asks its own (one letter a token, the softmax over the letters of the last row is what structured_outputs.choice leaves): the loop hands SP2's pending action to _force_close, where the KV holds the whole context and the end token was not taken; _ask_in_place settles the recurrent state as cache.capture does, copies it, forwards the hidden user turn (templates.hidden_turn with the question) after the KV's rows, reads the letters, and copies the state back and resets the KV's length (the rows above it are written over by the next forward). The drafter, ctx, usage and the client never see it. An answer other than supported continues the turn hidden at SP2 with that answer's notes text, as E1's hidden user turn: the end token is dropped, the note and the empty closed reasoning block are forwarded, the model goes on in the same response. Every other way out takes the end token as it was drawn, so the client receives what it would without the check: no claim, supported, an answer below its threshold, a failure of any kind (fail-open, claim_check(error:<why>)), the caps (acts_per_request, acts_per_session_hour; the check is not even asked when they leave no act), no room for the note, shadow. A request that records logprobs is never asked (its end token's row would be lost; claim_check(not_asked)).

The journal row (task E2, tier 1) has both answers with every option's probability, the structural twin (twin: no_run_after_last_write when no call after the last write matches run_tools, else ran), the since list, the class and ms. Every note, sent or in shadow the one that would have been, opens an outcome: once label_calls (8) tool calls followed it, or the next claim check of the session triggered, a PASS row at sp label (claim_outcome(fixed|ran_no_fix|no_run)) says whether a run-like call and a write followed and whether the claim came again; a fix after a note is a true positive, a run with no fix and the claim again a likely false positive. The policy file has E2 in shadow; a profile's tasks.E2 sets its mode (shipped: acting in coding, hermes and chat-app, shadow in overnight) and its claim_at and admit_at. A server whose stored monitor document predates E2 runs none of it until a version with the task is stored. With E2 off, or not triggered, every byte is the release's (tests/test_claim_check.py: off against no task over the handler, shadow and a supported claim against off on the chain, the tree and the single-token step, the engine's state equal before and after each question). On the served kernels (the fused GDN commit, a commit pending into the next verify, the verify graphs) tools/claim_identity.py asks the questions at each moment SP2 can meet (a partial accept and its rollback, a full accept, a tree commit, a decode step) and requires every later logit and state to be bit-identical to the run without them; it needs the GPU, so a hold runs it before E2 is switched on.

docs.title: Session-level tasks (SRV-121)
docs.text:
Three SP4 tasks look across turns. They read what a request carries about the turns before it, the model's tool calls (the assistant messages' tool_calls) and their results (the tool messages), each taken once per session by its call id, so a retried request counts nothing twice. Each acts with one PROMPT_TAIL_NOTE at the end of the prompt, and a request carries at most one of their notes, in the policy file's order:

task rule when the note (policy text) S2 context_health the monitor marked opencode's compaction request (no tools, the history as one user message; a client without a conversation id carries the mark to its next session key), and the first steps (2) tool-call steps after it read none of files (PROGRESS.yaml, AGENTS.md, SKILL.md) through read_tools, nor loaded a skill through skill_tools. Once per compaction; a step that reads one ends the watch (a PASS observation names it) "You are after a summary. Read PROGRESS.yaml and AGENTS.md before the next change." S1 gate_stagnation a checker gate failed fails (3) times in a row and the best later reading came less than min_improvement (10 %) of its distance to the limit closer than the first (15.6, 12.2, 3.5 improves; 3.5, 12.3, 3.5 does not). The checkers (pagodacheck, scenecheck, sketchcheck, calccheck, taskcheck), the gate label and the reading are patterns in the policy; a gate is checker + target + gate, so the same metric on two screenshots is two gates. Once per gate and stage, the stage being the next: line the state file last showed (read, or written by an edit); a PASS of the gate starts it over. Several stuck gates: one note naming the worst (farthest from its limit) "Gate (a) read 3.5, 12.3, 3.5. Record this stage as blocked in PROGRESS.yaml with the reason and take next." S4 stall_watchdog requests keep coming, but for minutes (20) no file changed (change: a write or edit whose result reads as done), nothing was committed (commit) and no checker number got 10 % closer to its limit or passed; again only after another minutes, and never within minutes of another session note "No progress for 20 minutes. Re-read PROGRESS.yaml and take the next stage." S5 turn_budget on every client and project (requires empty), three arms over the turn (the requests that carry the same last user message): repeat, the model's visible text between its tool calls states the same problem repeats (3) times among its last window (8) problem leads (the first sentence; similar 0.4 of their word 3-grams shared, a number in common when both name numbers, a problem word from cue), the count starting over after the note; first_write, a turn of a build class (classes: code_edit, design_ui, drawing, three_d) is first_write_s (180) seconds and first_write_steps (5) tool steps old and nothing the user asked for is written (a write tool's path, or a shell redirect into a file, outside the scratch directory, /tmp, logs and pid files), once a turn; wall_clock, a chat client (clients: open-webui) has had tool turns for minutes (12) with no product write for quiet_minutes (4), or for hard_minutes (18) in any case, then every again_minutes (4) the shorter again_text; verify (policy 7, 0.3.45-test), a build turn whose steps since its last product write wrote only scratch files, verify_scratch_writes (2) of them test tools (scripts or pages, not logs or data), verify_s (90) seconds or more after that write and 3 steps or more, once a turn (time alone is not a reason: opencode has no clock, a chat client has the wall clock's quiet rule) repeat: "Runtime note: you have now stated the same problem 3 times (\"…\") and the changes in between did not move it. Stop tuning it. If what fails is your own test tool … drop that test. Deliver what works: answer the user with what you built and where it is, what you verified and how, and what is still untested or failing. Do not change the product only to make your own test pass; if you did, say so." first_write: "… nothing the user asked for is written yet. Write the deliverable now, before any more setup …" wall_clock: "… the user is waiting in a chat for your answer. Finish now …" verify: "… your last N tool steps (M minutes) changed only test tooling, not the deliverable. Stop building test tools. … run one check with a tool that already works here … then answer …"

S1, S2 and S4 stay silent on a request that offers no tools and in a project whose system prompt does not match requires (PROGRESS\.yaml): a project without state files. S5 (0.3.43-test, SRV-179 and SRV-181; the UT2 self-test: an Open WebUI agent chat had a working game after 25 minutes, then wrote "The bot is stuck at x=436" seven times while it tuned its own playtest bot and never answered in 43 minutes; an opencode one-file page was written at 642 s of 733 s, after a Firefox rig and three hung servers) needs no state file and runs under every profile that runs the monitor, in the document's mode (the profiles' task table does not list it). Replayed on that chat, it adds the first-write note at 3.1 minutes, the wrap-up at 18.0 and the repeat note at the third "stuck at x=436" lead (36.0 minutes); on four clean opencode runs (a bug fix, a refactor, a duplicate finder, a fix with tests) it adds nothing. A box whose monitor policy is a stored document gets the task with tools/monitor_migrate.py --put http://127.0.0.1:8000. The midnight date line in opencode's system prompt is a prompt change, not a compaction.

The client that has gone: when no request comes for S4's minutes after a turn ended, nothing can act in band. The watch (Monitor.sweep, every --conductor-watch-s seconds, 30 by default, on its own thread) journals one event a turn end, task S4 at sp watch, reason client_gone(N min): PASS with notify: off, or NOTIFY when the policy's notify.enabled is on (in shadow NOTIFY is journaled as "would", never sent). A push goes to notify.url, or to $TANDEM_NOTIFY_URL when the policy leaves it empty (the shipped policy does), with the token read from notify.token_file (~/.qwen38-spark-engine/conductor/ntfy.token on the box; never in the policy, the journal or a log) and the CA in ca_file; its result ("sent 200", "failed: no url", "failed: no token file") is in the event's detail. notify.enabled is off in ops/supervisor.yaml; a profile's context.notify sets it, on only in the overnight profile (decided 2026-09-30). A server with the fake engine never pushes.

The state is per session (SessionState.tasks), hashes, numbers and file names only. GET /v1/conductor/watch lists it per session: each gate's readings and whether it was noted, a compaction being watched and its steps, the minutes since progress and what it was, the client's idle minutes and whether it has gone, and whether a push would go out; the dashboard's Monitor screen shows it every 5 s. A profile's context section sets S1's fails (s1_runs), S4's minutes (s4_minutes) and notify.enabled (notify); the task modes come from its tasks as for every task (overnight: S1, S2, S4 act; coding and chat: off).

docs.title: Observability (SRV-115)
docs.text:
One journal for the router and the monitor: the table conductor_events in the usage ledger's file (schema version 2, migrated in place at start, every old row kept; python tools/ledger_migrate_check.py LEDGER tries it on a copy), written from its own queue thread, never on the decode thread. A router row (kind route) per TandemLLM request; a monitor row (kind monitor) per decision with its task and tier, its mode and rule, its reason and action, the hidden text (stored once in conductor_texts by its hash), its tokens, its position and the reasoning tokens at a cut; the request's outcome fills its rows when it ends, and the next request's checker result (RESULT: PASS|FAIL <- ...) fills next_checker. Checks that find nothing are counted, not stored (an answer whose calls all passed is one row, journal.tool_passes). Rows and texts older than 30 days go nightly, and the ledger's weekly backup leaves both tables out. With the ledger off the journal lives in memory; with the conductor raw nothing is written.

The ledger's requests gains conductor_acts, conductor_hidden_tokens and conductor_acted; the dashboard's speed figures leave out the requests the conductor acted in. Prometheus (qse_conductor_*, METRICS.md) counts every decision, passes included, the actions, the hidden tokens, the gave-ups, the tier 1 questions and their failures, and the reasoning tokens cut. The live event (contract 1.2) carries activity.conductor on a watched request, with supervising while a hidden forward runs. GET /v1/conductor/events lists the monitor's decisions, and a session's timeline and export hold both halves.

docs.title: Extending it
docs.text:
The interface the conductor's policy engine builds on, kept stable:

  • A rule: tier0.register(name, safe_point, params, required, doc) on fn(event, task, sup) -> Action | None. params is the JSON Schema of the task's parameters; the policy schema picks it up. A task in the file names the rule (rule: name) and carries its parameters, texts included.
  • The events (tandemapp/conductor/monitor/observe.py): RequestEvent (SP4, and sup.req at every later point: messages, tools, tool_choice, n, prompt tokens, in_think, max_tokens, the client's own budget, the client kind, whether a grammar constrains the answer, the profile), BlockEvent (reasoning tokens, inside, the detector arm that fired, the history arm's share, the position), FinishEvent (inside, the answer so far, the position), ToolCallEvent (name, arguments, index; for a block that does not parse its text and the parser's reason; the tool's schema; final when nothing can be written again).
  • An SP3 rule returns REPAIR_CALL with detail["arguments"] (a call) or detail["calls"] (a block that did not parse), REGENERATE_CALL whose text is the reminder, GIVE_UP, or PASS with a reason (an observation); detail["mode"] lowers what one finding may do. Supervisor.check_answer(items) runs them; release_call / release_block hand out what goes.
  • Action(kind, reason, text, budget, score, detail) from policy.ACTIONS. SET_THINK_BUDGET with budget=0 turns thinking off; with budget=n the request's reasoning closes after n tokens with the action's text, which must contain the closer.
  • Monitor(mode, policy, tok): .begin(mode, req, prompt_ids, conv_id) gives the request's Supervisor (None when raw), .reload(policy) swaps the policy for requests that start later, .mode_for(header, n) lowers a mode. A supervisor's .session is the session's state; .memo is a rule's per-request scratch.
  • The journal: Journal.write(event); Journal.sinks are called with every event (the SQLite journal's monitor_sink, Prometheus's on_conductor_event), and with three bookkeeping events: OUTCOME (the request ended), LABEL (a later checker result), COUNTS (the checks that found nothing).

docs.title: The Chat tab and chatd
docs.text:
The Chat tab and chatd are in beta.

The dashboard's Chat tab (#/chat) is a chat with history whose runs live on the server: close the browser in the middle of an answer, open the chat on a phone, and it shows the answer at the token the engine is writing now and keeps streaming. The wire contract is dashboard/src/chat/CONTRACT.md; this page is how it runs on a box.

docs.title: What runs where
docs.text:
browser  --https-->  engine server :8000  --/v1/chat-app/* (auth checked, byte forward)-->  chatd 127.0.0.1:8016
                                                                                           |  ~/.tandemllm/chat/chat.sqlite3
                                                                                           |  POST /v1/chat/completions --> :8000
  • chatd (python -m chatd, the chatd/ package): a standard-library Python process. It holds the stream to the engine, so a run does not end when a browser closes; it writes every change of a conversation to an event log with a sequence number, and a device attaches with a snapshot and then tails the log from the snapshot's seq (SSE, Last-Event-ID on a reconnect, event: reset for a device more than 2,000 events behind).
  • The forward (tandemapp/chat_forward.py): the engine server (and the standalone proxy, tandem-app) passes /v1/chat-app/* to chatd after the dashboard's auth check. chatd answers only requests that carry the forward key.
  • The model is reached as any client reaches it, through POST /v1/chat/completions with x-session-id: chat-<conversation id>, so the engine's park, spill and live rows follow the chat. What a model can do comes from /v1/models (the tandem card, models/<id>/card.json), never from a model name.

chatd never imports the engine and an engine restart does not touch it: a run that loses the engine retries with backoff for 10 minutes, then ends interrupted with its text kept, and Continue resumes it. Stopping chatd ends its open runs interrupted the same way. A call the engine refuses for memory (503, "needs ... GiB with every cache given back") is retried once after its Retry-After, then the chat is compacted and the smaller prompt sent; from then on the chat compacts at 80 % of the refused size, not only of the window. A 400 that says the request is over the model's context window (a tool result grew it past the guard's estimate) compacts the chat and sends the call once more when the compaction made it smaller; when it cut nothing, or the smaller call is refused too, the run fails with the engine's message. Stop also ends a call whose response has not started, such as one the engine holds while it waits for memory and sends no headers: chatd shuts the connection, the message ends stopped, and the engine books the request abandoned (SRV-777).

One step's tool results share the room the model has left (#18): half of what is left under the compaction line, 2,000 tokens at least, never past the window less twice the answer's room, and never more than 64,000 characters a result (12,000 in Agents mode). read_file cuts at whole lines and says where to go on ("[truncated at 64,000 characters: lines 1-30 of 317 shown, 639,237 more bytes; read on with offset=31]"); a line longer than one read goes on with its column argument. A file over 4 MiB is read 4 MiB at a time from the line offset names, numbered as in the file, and the marker names the bytes after the page ("[lines 80000-80002 shown of a 6,749,998-byte file, 749,845 more bytes after them; read on with offset=80003]"), so no part of it is out of reach (SRV-651). grep takes a folder or one file and reads every file the same way, a MiB at a time: it searches a line's first 64 K characters and a file's first 16 MiB, and says when the rest of a file is unread; one call gets 10 s across all its files and ends with "partial results" when that runs out. Its line numbers are the ones read_file shows (SRV-649). Other results keep their first and last quarter and the whole output under .tandem/outputs/. A request's estimate carries a margin for the text the engine has not counted yet (15 % of it): at the edge our engine counts the request exactly (POST /v1/tokenize) and a request over the window fails before it is sent, with the count; a relayed model gets a max_tokens that leaves the margin free.

File texts stay out of the request: a finished write_file's content, and an edit_file's old or new text over 2,000 characters, go to the model as a stub (path, lines, bytes, sha256 and the read_file call that shows it) from the next request on; the store and the thread keep the text. A worker's (Agents mode) stay whole until a compaction, which stubs them: the engine holds the rows of the call, and a stub inside its last answer made the next call read that answer again. A read_file or bash result over 4,000 characters stays whole until a compaction, which stubs it (a read names its read_file call; a command keeps its first and last lines), so a request only ever changes at its tail between compactions and the engine's prefix cache holds the rest. A compaction lands under half the limit that set it off: a long run keeps fewer than its last three steps until it does. The [compact] log line and the Context panel give the chat's request size before and after, and the summary call's size apart.

docs.title: Memory priority
docs.text:
Each chat has a priority for the engine's memory: high, normal or low (0.15.3, #169). Normal is the default. The tools pill in the composer's options row ("3 tools") opens a menu with a Memory priority row of three buttons. When several chats need more memory than the box has, the higher one goes first, and a chat that waits moves up a step every 30 minutes. When memory is short, the engine gives back a low chat's idle conversation before a normal one's.

chatd keeps the value in the chat's settings (priority, through PATCH /conversations/{id}/settings; any other value is a 400) and sends it to the engine as tandem.priority on each call, high and low only. A normal chat sends nothing, which the engine reads as normal. Only waits for memory use it; a chat runs no faster for it. parallel-requests.md has the engine's side.
