QWEN38_NOTES_HEAD_ORDER=memory (the default) puts the memory card and the index before the class note, which differs by class; class puts the class note first (before SRV-765). An index in that head names its routes on <address>; with a shell the session's own address ({tandem_url}, .../s/<token>) comes in a tail note once a session, so the index is the same text in every chat (QWEN38_MEMORY_ROUTES=auto, the default: this layout only where the index goes in the head, the first turn of a conversation on the engine's own prompt; an index at the tail, QWEN38_NOTES_HEAD=off included, names the session's address itself, as before SRV-765). note uses the address note wherever the index goes; index never does (no two chats share the head then). A head note that still carries the session's token (a class note whose package names {tandem_url} or {tandem_scratch}) is named in the turn's extra.head_session;
  • the matching notes, on a new user message (never a tool turn): BM25 over the message, at most 3 notes that share at least 2 of its words, within 600 tokens. On a session's first turn they go in after the index. Their note has its own frame: the router's wrapper says "do not mention it", these are the user's notes, so the frame and its head tell the model to answer from a note that answers the message, to say it comes from its notes (a ratified note is confirmed by the user), and to tell the user both when the files disagree.

Memory also needs a place for the notes in the served model's prompt: the end of the last message, before its <|im_end|>. A model whose template ends no message with a token has none, and its adapter's conductor fit says so (notes: false, chat-mode.md). Flint's template is such a one (a message runs until the next role token), so on Flint no profile reads or writes notes: each turn's decision row has extra.memory = {mode: off, why: model_notes}, no memory card, index or body goes in, the model writes no block and the background writer has no session to write. Before 0.14.2 those turns said memory: on with the error no_insertion_point (SRV-703). The Notes tab's "Where memory is on" panel names the served model when it reads no note, and every profile with its switch and its clients (where in GET /v1/conductor/memory/notes).

Laya's question "does this message ask to remember, forget or recall" attaches the long memory skill (settings.memory.notes.intent, shadow by default: journaled only).

On the first turn of a session, and again after a compaction, the model gets the index: the pinned ratified rules, then one line per note the request may see, within 1,500 tokens.

docs.title: The background writer
docs.text:
Besides the blocks in its answers, a session's facts are written by a hidden turn of Qwen itself, thinking off, on the conversation the engine already holds (tandemapp/conductor/memwriter.py, server/app.py memory_once). settings.memory.notes.writer: mode off (the default), shadow (the turn runs, its blocks are counted, nothing is stored) or on.

  • The triggers: the session's end (no request for idle_s, 180 s, and min_new_tokens new since its last pass), a GIVE_UP, and a compaction. With after_compaction: idle (the default) the compaction's turn waits for the next idle moment like the others; with turn it runs right after the summary, before the engine goes to the next request (at most turn_deadline_s). A compaction served as a guest (a short prompt) has no record in place; its mark waits for the idle look.
  • The record: the session's last generation (its end anchor), else the last prompt in the rows up to its last message's end.
  • The gate: Laya's "do these messages contain something to remember" on the session's last user messages; a no at 0.6 or more skips the turn. Not asked after a compaction in the turn (the decider asks only while no request holds the engine).
  • The turn's prompt carries the notes that already match the session, so it updates instead of adding. Its output is parsed as the inline blocks are; a tandem_memory tool call (Qwen writes the call form when the session's tools are in the record) counts as its block. Notes land as writer: qwen-writer, provisional.
  • Any other tool call ends the turn at its function's name (after a compaction Qwen answered an empty or a bash call). The run then says what NONE says: none: true, with answer (none, empty, tool_call) and cut (the function's name, or empty); the log line reads wrote: NONE (tool_call: bash, cut).
  • A request that arrives stops the turn at its next chunk; the conversation's rows and anchors stay as they were.
  • The writer's last look is in its stats (GET /v1/conductor/memory/notes/writes, writer.last_look), and the log says [memory] writer look: hold (or gpu, nothing, moved) when a due session cannot be written, and writer look: no session once when the resident conversation never came with a memory session (no session id, raw, a profile with memory off, or a model that reads no note). Inside a hold the box lock is held and every look is hold: a test engine in a hold needs its own BOX_LOCK.
  • QWEN38_MEMORY_WRITER_TEXT: a file a test engine appends each writer turn's text to. Never set it on the service; the text is the session's.
  • Its own NONE (0.3.35-test): ban_tool_call (on by default) adds a logit bias of -100 to the <tool_call> token for the writer's turn, so a call cannot start; the cut above stays as the backstop. prefill (empty by default) is text the answer starts with; its tokens follow the generation prompt. The run records ban (the token ids, or unavailable) and prefill (its token count).
  • Shadow (0.3.35-test): what a shadow run would write, each block after the secret-pattern refusal, is appended to <user>/shadow/writer-<yyyy-mm-dd>.md (0600). Nothing reads it back; the store reads only user/, projects/ and sessions/, and the user's delete removes it with the rest.

Measured on a test engine (the 0.4.0 series, a synthetic 10-turn coding session, low effort, writer on): the writer at the session's end wrote 2 notes in 7.6 s for 282 tokens from a 5,374-token record. A new session that asked what was remembered got 1,781 prompt tokens with memory on (the index and 3 notes) against 136 off, and its first token in 0.97 s against 0.39 s; the answer named both rules the user had asked to keep. Decode was 99.7 ms a block with memory on and 99.6 off (measured).

docs.title: Behind the proxy
docs.text:
For a backend behind the proxy (vLLM, SGLang, any OpenAI-compatible server, a cloud API) the same turn is one more request to the backend the session used (proxy/memwriter.py): the messages of the session's last request as they were sent (the notes in place, so the backend's prefix cache matches), its answer's text, and the writer's user turn. Thinking is off, the session's tools stay in the body with tool_choice: "none" (ban_tool_call), and prefill is an assistant start where the backend can continue one (vLLM, SGLang). The answer goes through the engine writer's parser, store and journal; the run says via: proxy, backend, model, cost_micros, and the request is a ledger row of the client harness:writer (the Backends screen counts it under memory).

  • When: the session's end (idle_s, min_new_tokens) and the client's compaction request in the same session (the session's last turn before it is the record, kept apart from the turns after it). One writer request at a time, only while the backend has no client request in flight. On a local backend a client request that arrives stops the writer's stream (the connection is closed, the session stays due); a cloud request runs to its end.
  • The switches, per backend (harness document, TANDEM_BACKEND_<ID>_WRITER*): writer auto (on, but off on a paid cloud model: a cloud backend whose model has no price or a price above zero), off, shadow, on; writer_usd_day (0.25 USD) the spend a day on a paid model, checked against an estimate before each run (the prompt at the input price, max_tokens at the output price), null for none; writer_runs_day (48); writer_prompt_tokens (32,000 estimated; the oldest messages after the system prompt are dropped first). The effective mode is the lower of the backend's and settings.memory.notes.writer.mode. A paid model without a price is refused (no_price). Refusals are journaled once per record (cap_runs, cap_cost, no_price, too_long, http_<status>); the day's runs and spend come back from the ledger after a restart. The Backends API shows the mode per model (writer.mode, writer.why), the day's figures, the settings document's mode (writer.settings_mode) and where a shadow run's blocks go (writer.shadow_log). The Backends screen sets the four switches on a backend's form (a PATCH of harness.writer*, only the fields that changed; a field a variable sets is locked) and shows each model's resolved mode on the backend's page.

docs.title: What is journaled
docs.text:
The Notes tab's counts (GET /v1/conductor/memory/notes, memory): index_notes counts the notes each injected index listed, body_notes the note bodies that went in. Before 0.3.39-test a first turn counted both as the index, so a session whose body went in read body_notes 0.

Kind memory_notes: each write (write, api_write: op, id, scope, kind, why it was refused, redaction counts), each injection (injected: the note ids), the dashboard's edits (human), the nightly job. Never a title or a body.

docs.title: Monitoring: several engines and the machines behind them
docs.text:
With more than one backend, the dashboard answers three questions for all of them at once: what each request is doing right now, how each engine is doing inside, and how the machine behind it is doing. Each answer has its own source, and each source is optional. All of it is measured or null, never estimated: a figure a backend does not report reads “not reported by this backend”.

layer where it reads what it gives needs the relay every answer the proxy relays per request: tokens from usage, cached and reasoning tokens where reported, TTFT and decode rate at the proxy, cost nothing L1: the engine's page vLLM's and SGLang's /metrics, every 15 s per engine: requests running and waiting, KV use, decode rate, prefix-cache hits, TTFT, queue and prefill percentiles, preemptions, speculation kind vllm or sglang; SGLang --enable-metrics L2: the plugin a plugin inside vLLM or SGLang, posting once a second per request: the engine's own queue, prefill and decode time, cached tokens, preemptions, finish reason the plugin and two variables the host collector the machine behind each backend memory, CPU, GPUs, disks, network, the process behind each backend's port nothing here; a collector or exporters on a remote machine

The four layers TandemApp reads.

docs.title: Every request at once
docs.text:
Performance, Parallel (#/performance?tab=parallel) shows every request in flight on every backend, the engine included. It reads GET /v1/dashboard/parallel once a second; the server builds the document at most every 0.4 s for all viewers, and a poll with since carries only the new samples.

The Performance view, Parallel page: every request in flight on six backends, the aggregate decode rate, and one card per backend. Demo data from the dashboard's mock server (npm run preview:mock), not a measurement.

  • The aggregate decode rate now, and its last five minutes stacked by backend.
  • The requests by state: waiting, prefilling, thinking, tool call, writing.
  • The time to first token at p50 and p90, the cache hit and the cost per minute, over the requests finished in the last five minutes.
  • One card per backend.
  • One lane per request: backend and model, client, session, state, tokens with thinking apart, decode tok/s now and on average, TTFT, prefill rate, cache, cost so far, elapsed. A lane keeps its row until a few seconds after it ends.

A lane's live token count comes from the best source the backend allows. The engine's own requests use the engine's count. A TandemLLM backend behind a proxy is read from that engine's own board once a second, because the relay tags each request with X-Tandem-Relay-Id; the engine streams blocks of several tokens, so its frames are not a count. Any other backend's stream frames count only after they were checked: each finished streamed answer's frames are compared with its usage.completion_tokens (within 2 tokens and 1 %), answers with and without tool calls apart, and two passing answers of a kind with no failure among the last 8 make the frames a count. DeepSeek's reasoning and content frames are one token each; its tool-call arguments arrive several tokens a frame, so a DeepSeek lane has no live count while it writes a call. Without a count a lane shows its frames and “not reported”, and its tokens arrive with the usage at the end.

agent-like sessions at once 8 16 32 aggregate tok/s, all lanes 526 896 1,495

A load test of the Parallel view, not an engine benchmark: N agent-like sessions (a system prompt, two tools, up to three streamed turns) through a test proxy in front of a cloud API, the engine and two fake backends, 0 errors in each run. The aggregate is the sum over every backend. Measured: tools/parallel_load.py, the 0.4.0 series. With 32 streams the page's document took about 1 ms to build and a poll was at most 55 KB.

tools/parallel_load.py drives the page on your own backends, for example --mix deepseek-flash=10,TandemLLM=2 --duration 90 --budget-usd 0.5 --board. It reports TTFT, decode rate, cache hit, throughput and cost per model, stops starting turns at the budget, and with --board puts the page's per-second series beside the frames its own clients received.

docs.title: Inside vLLM and SGLang: the engine's page (L1)
docs.text:
For a backend of kind vllm or sglang the proxy reads the engine's /metrics every 15 s through a name table checked against vLLM v0.30.0 and SGLang v0.5.21 (proxy/engines.py). Window figures come from the first and the newest reading of the last 5 minutes; with one reading, or no traffic in the window, they are null. A family a release renamed maps to nothing and its tile says “not reported by this backend”: a new release can cost a tile, never a failed read. After a failed read the proxy waits 30 s, then 60, then 120 s.

figure vLLM SGLang running, waiting vllm:num_requests_running, _waiting sglang:num_running_reqs, num_queue_reqs KV in use vllm:kv_cache_usage_perc sglang:token_usage decode rate vllm:generation_tokens_total over the window sglang:generation_tokens_total, gen_throughput prefix-cache hits vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total over queries_total sglang:cached_tokens_total over prompt_tokens_total queue, prefill, decode vllm:request_queue_time_seconds and siblings sglang:queue_time_seconds only preemptions vllm:num_preemptions_total sglang:num_retracted_requests_total speculation drafts, draft tokens, accepted tokens, and acceptance per draft position sglang:spec_accept_rate, spec_accept_length

The engine figures and the families they come from.

The proxy's own /metrics carries the mapped families as qse_backend_* with a backend label, for a Prometheus of your own; they never enter the engine's own families. Mapping one page of about 500 lines takes about 2 ms on the poller's own thread, and a relay thread never waits for it.

docs.title: Inside vLLM and SGLang: the plugins (L2)
docs.text:
The page gives totals. A single request's queue time, its prefill time and whether the scheduler preempted it are not on it. Two small packages in plugins/ run inside the engine and send those numbers per request:

pip install plugins/vllm    # tandemllm-vllm-plugin, into vLLM's own Python
pip install plugins/sglang  # tandemllm-sglang-plugin, into SGLang's own Python
TANDEM_COLLECT_URL=http://proxy-host:8080/v1/collect/<backend id>
TANDEM_COLLECT_TOKEN=<the proxy's collect token>

vLLM loads its plugin from the vllm.stat_logger_plugins entry point, once per data-parallel engine in its API server process; SGLang loads its plugin from sglang.srt.plugins in every process it starts, with two hooks on its tokenizer manager and its scheduler's metrics collector. Neither package has a dependency, and neither reads a prompt, an answer or a token id: each item is counts and times. A plugin keeps the last 10,000 finished requests and 300 one-second scheduler samples in memory and posts what is new once a second, or an empty batch every 10 s when the engine is idle. The collect token is TANDEM_COLLECT_TOKEN in the proxy's environment, or one the proxy makes and stores in its config database at the first need; it lets its holder post numbers for a backend that exists, nothing else.

The proxy joins each item to the request's ledger row by an id it sends upstream: vLLM gets X-Request-Id: px-<hex> and reports chatcmpl-px-<hex>; SGLang gets rid in the body. A client that sets its own id keeps it, and the join uses it. The row then gets the engine's own queue_ms, prompt_ms, decode_ms, decode_tps, prefill_tps, cached_tokens, preemptions and engine_finish, and l2_join says exact. A request the proxy cannot tag (the Responses API, SGLang with n above 1) is matched by time and token counts when exactly one row fits, and says approximate. An item waits up to 10 minutes for its row, and a row for its item.

The engine always starts. If the plugin does not fit a release, vLLM's loader logs the import error and starts without it, SGLang skips a renamed hook target, and a failing hook is logged at most once a minute and switches itself off after 100 failures in a row. The backend's card says “L2 plugin” while batches arrive and “L1 only” after 60 s without one.

docs.title: The machine behind each backend
docs.text:
The System view lists the machines: this one first, with the server's own process, then the machine behind each backend, down to the process behind the backend's port. For a vLLM on the same machine that is its API server and its engine core, with their RSS, CPU, threads, uptime and GPU memory. A backend's host setting says where to read it:

setting reads per process auto this machine when the backend's URL is loopback or one of its addresses; nothing for a cloud API yes same this machine, whatever the URL says yes collector tandem-app hostcollect on the backend's machine yes exporter a node_exporter page and a DCGM exporter page no off nothing

A backend's host setting.

On a remote machine, run the collector next to the backend and give both sides the same token:

# on the backend's machine
TANDEM_COLLECTOR_TOKEN=$(openssl rand -hex 24) tandem-app hostcollect --host 0.0.0.0 --port 9108
# on the proxy's machine
TANDEM_COLLECTOR_TOKEN=<the same token>
TANDEM_BACKEND_VLLM1_HOST=collector
TANDEM_BACKEND_VLLM1_HOST_URL=http://gpu-host:9108

The collector answers GET /host as JSON and GET /metrics as Prometheus text (tandem_host_*), both behind the bearer token. It refuses to bind beyond loopback without one, because its answer names processes and their command lines. Command lines show the home as ~, and the value after any flag whose name holds key, token, secret, passw or auth is masked. A remote read runs on its own thread, so a slow or dead host never holds the page.

On a GB10 the CPU and the GPU share one memory pool. The driver reports no memory for the GPU itself, so the view shows “unified” there and MemAvailable is the figure to watch. Nothing is sampled while nobody looks: when the System view asks, the collector reads at most every 5 s and scans the processes at most every 15 s. Measured on a DGX Spark against the running engine: one sample with a process scan cost 7.46 ms of CPU, 0.050 % of a core at that cadence; the memory figures equalled /proc/meminfo to the byte, and the engine's GPU memory equalled nvidia-smi's within 49,152 bytes of 81.7 GB (measured, the 0.4.0 series).

docs.title: Your own Prometheus
docs.text: The controller's /metrics (the metrics:read permission: a viewer's session or an API token with that scope, docs/auth.md) carries its own families (qse_proxy_requests_total, qse_proxy_tokens_total, qse_proxy_cost_micros_total, qse_proxy_ttft_seconds, qse_backend_up, qse_backend_inflight and more), the mapped engine families as qse_backend_*, and the plugin's age and joins. The collector's /metrics carries tandem_host_*. reference/metrics.md lists every family registered in the code.

docs.title: Packages
docs.text: A package is what the conductor attaches to a turn by class: instructions the model follows, references it can read, and an eval set that says whether it helped. The shipped packages live under packages/ (chat-mode.md says how the router injects them and how the library is searched). This page lists the first packages of OPS-39, their shape, and how each one is measured. Nothing below is measured yet: every line says so.

docs.title: The shape of a package folder
docs.text:
packages/system/<name>/    a system package: PACKAGE.md (the text that goes in, whole), manifest.json, eval/, references/
packages/library/<name>/   a first package: SKILL.md (body before `## Reference` goes in; the reference on request),
                               manifest.json, references/*.md, exemplars/*, eval/prompts.jsonl, eval/rubric.md
  • manifest.json: name, version, kind, description, max_tokens (the cap of the text that goes in), general, library, requires_tools, fallback, the classes, the files, the eval set (its prompts, rubric, count, checks, human sample), calibration (a box-dependent threshold such as fps_min, written once by the calibration run), measured (null until a run exists), signature (the system set is signed at install, OPS-31).
  • eval/prompts.jsonl: one prompt a line, {id, class, prompt, checks, terms?, ...}. Prompts are original (adapted, never copied), free of owner names, hosts and paths; tools/packages_first.py checks that.
  • eval/rubric.md: the automatic checks and the judge items in the format of the eval-judge package (packages/system/eval-judge/references/rubric-format.md).
  • deliverable (in packages/seed.json, SRV-615): what the package's result is for when a tool can make it, send, schedule or post. write-message and formal-letter carry send; event-plan, weekly-schedule and checklist-builder schedule; social-post post. On a request that offers a client tool whose declaration makes that result (a recipient and a message for send, a time and a subject for schedule; a post counts as a send), such a package gets one more side question before it goes in: does the user want it done with a tool, or the text itself? Without such a tool nothing is asked and the package goes in. On tool it stays out; the journal row's package_choice.kept_out names it with the tools whose declaration makes the deliverable (signals.tool_effects). The router's tool_fit.deliverable is shadow as shipped (journals under shadow.tools.kept_out, changes nothing), on or off.
  • packages/seed.json registers every package; packages/library/INDEX.md names a library skill's classes. The router (tandemapp/conductor/schema.py, SHIPPED_ROUTER) lists a package on the classes whose package question may pick it, or on every turn of a class when it is general.

The texts are written for a small model: numbered steps, one instruction a line, concrete defaults, a Do/Don't pair per key rule, a "Done when" list the model can run. The injected part stays short (a library skill's body within the house 350 tokens); the detail is in the ## Reference (served by GET /v1/library/<name>) and in references/ and exemplars/ (read through package_read once the tool server of SRV-105 exists).

docs.title: The first packages
docs.text:
package kind goes in cap needs what it teaches eval measured tandem-core system, general on every class but summarize whole 300 nothing the runtime's conventions: typed tool arguments, no think tags in text, one answer a turn, size limits, the stop rule for long files, a plain final answer 8 prompts, automatic checks only not measured render-tools system, general on the classes that build whole 750 render when to render, what to fix first (errors, motion, fps, sound, picture), three renders an answer, the CDN allowlist, the tool names of SRV-105 6 prompts not measured; the tool server does not exist, so no chat offers render and the tool fit leaves it out eval-judge system, routed by no class whole 900 nothing the judge prompt: five items 1 to 5 from three frames and the probes, one JSON object, the same scores for the same input 6 described cases not measured creative-coding library skill (drawing, three_d, code_edit, design_ui) body 350 nothing one-file visuals with sound: a three-line plan, the hard rules (one file, seed, keys, WebAudio on a gesture), defaults; reference: skeleton, sound, easing, palettes; files: particles and boids, WebAudio patterns, pixel sprites, a Three.js skeleton, a 120-line exemplar 24 prompts not measured charts library skill (drawing, design_ui, code_edit, research) body 350 nothing an SVG chart from the prompt's data in the house style, every value as text, counted back; reference: the SVG grammar per form; file: the chart grammar 20 prompts with data; prompt_terms reads every value back not measured voxel-worlds library skill (three_d, code_edit) body 350 nothing the voxel build order with a render after each feature, the frame-rate rule, a to-do file, a seed; reference: rng, voxels, meshes, day-night, a state machine, audio, presets; files: six curated modules and two exemplars (prompt, plan, diff) 20 prompts, one a six-feature sequence scored on the sixth's frame rate not measured explainer-video library skill (drawing, code_edit) body 350 render_video a scene script and a cue list for the render_video tool, the return's checks, the honesty rules (every number names its source, schematics say so); reference: the fields; files: a 30-second example, the tool's interface spec 12 prompts not measured; without the tool its fallback explainer-video-script goes in

Tokens are counted on the engine's tokenizer with python tools/packages_first.py --tokenizer <dir>; the table's caps are the manifests'.

docs.title: How a package is measured
docs.text:
The method is the eval of VIS-E6: for a package P and its eval set, two sides on the same build in the same hour, one request at a time, the lookup store scrubbed of the eval outputs, the order alternating off/on per prompt:

  • off: tandem-core only, greedy, thinking off, max_tokens 24,000, seed 42;
  • on: the same request with P; when P needs the render tool the on side is an agent turn with at most 3 render calls;
  • a third row, "off with tools", separates the tool's effect from the instructions'.

Reported per package: pass rate (every automatic check passed), judge score (eval-judge, the served model through its image input, temperature 0), the human score on the ten-prompt sample (blind, the reviewer named), the three deltas, tokens and tok/s per side, renders per prompt. A run records the build, the profile digest, the package version, the date and hour, the judge version and the raw JSON's hash. The table goes into the package's note, append-only, and the dashboard tile shows pass 17/20 · judge 3.8/5 · +0.9 vs off · <date>; without a run it shows "not measured". A surprising delta is "needs verification" until a second run in another hour agrees.

The fps_min threshold is calibrated on the box once (the exemplar page at 640x360 on the box's software WebGL, minus 20 %) and written into the manifest's calibration; a package without a calibration record fails that check.

Until the tool server (SRV-105) and the harness (OPS-37) exist, the sets and the rubrics are the deliverable, and every gain a package is expected to bring is a hypothesis.

docs.title: The plugin SDK
docs.text:
tandemapp_plugin is a small Python package for writing TandemApp plugins: it reads the requests of the plugin host, calls your functions and writes the answers, so a plugin is a few decorated functions instead of a JSON-RPC reader. It uses the standard library only and lives in sdk/python.

Two complete plugins are built on it: note-webhook (an observer hook and a tool that post notes to a webhook) and keyword-router (a decision provider for the conductor's classify and judge questions). The tests install and run both through the plugin host.

docs.title: Start a plugin
docs.text:
pip install sdk/python                   # or: PYTHONPATH=sdk/python python -m tandemapp_plugin ...
tandemapp-plugin new my-tool             # --kind tool (default), hook or provider; --trust host
python tools/plugin_check.py my-tool     # the install's own checks, nothing installed

new writes the folder my-tool/ with plugin.json, main.py and a copy of the SDK (tandemapp_plugin/), and never writes into a folder that exists. A sandboxed plugin sees only its own tree, so the SDK travels inside it: tandemapp-plugin vendor <folder> copies it again after an SDK update, and tandemapp-plugin check <folder> says when a copy is out of date or a declared tool would be refused.

Then install it like any plugin: POST /v1/fleet/plugins {"source": {"type": "folder", "path": ...}}, grant what it asks for, enable it (plugins). Sign it with tools/plugin_sign.py when it should run at trust host on a signature (signing).

docs.title: A plugin
docs.text:
import os, sys
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))   # the SDK copy beside it
from tandemapp_plugin import Plugin, ToolError

plugin = Plugin()                     # reads plugin.json beside the script

@plugin.tool("greet", description="Say hello to someone by name.",
             input_schema={"type": "object", "properties": {"name": {"type": "string"}},
                           "required": ["name"], "additionalProperties": False},
             read_only=True, destructive=False, idempotent=True, open_world=False)
def greet(args, ctx):
    if not args["name"].strip():
        raise ToolError("a name, please")            # answered with isError
    return f"{plugin.settings.get('greeting', 'Hello')}, {args['name']}."

if __name__ == "__main__":
    plugin.main()

The manifest still declares every contribution (the manifest): the host offers only what plugin.json declares, with the manifest's schema. plugin.main() first compares the two (plugin.check()) and refuses to start when they differ, one line a difference on stderr, so a schema changed in one place and not the other shows in the plugin's log instead of as a refused call.

docs.title: Contributions
docs.text:
decorator the handler gets it returns @plugin.tool(name, description=, input_schema=, read_only=, destructive=, idempotent=, open_world=, title=None) (args, ctx): the arguments, already checked against the schema by the host text, a list of MCP content items, a full result {content, ...}, or any JSON value (sent as text and structuredContent); raise ToolError(text) for an error result @plugin.hook(name) (call, ctx): call.event at the hook's payload level, call.stage, call.mode, call.request, call.hook a hooks-v1 result {action: continue \| modify \| deny \| decide, patch?, decision?, reason?, labels?}, or None for continue @plugin.decision(provider, question=) (ask, ctx): ask.question, ask.options, ask.text (redacted or full) or ask.chars (meta), ask.instructions, ask.model, ask.deadline_ms {label, confidence?, probabilities?} or the label; the label must be one of ask.options @plugin.backend(name) (req, ctx): req.method, req.path, req.body {status, body}, or {status, events: [...]} for a stream

A provider registers once per question it answers, so one function can serve a question and another the next. ctx.plugin is the plugin and ctx.id the host's request id.

The four annotations. A tool states read_only, destructive, idempotent and open_world (MCP's readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint), each true or false, and an input schema of type object that says "additionalProperties": false on every object in it, nested ones, array items and $defs it refers to included. The decorator refuses a tool that misses one (ToolDefinitionError, naming the annotation or the place in the schema), as the install would. validate_tool(tool) gives the same lines for a tool written as a dict, e.g. one of a manifest.

docs.title: What a plugin may ask
docs.text:
what needs plugin.settings its settings as the host passed them at start, each default filled in nothing plugin.read_settings() its settings as they are now (tandem/settings) settings:read plugin.secret(name) a secret granted to it: from its environment, else asked of the host (tandem/secret); None when granted and not set secrets:<name> plugin.engine(params) engine control (tandem/engine) refused until engine control for plugins exists plugin.request(method, params) any request of the plugin's to the host its capability plugin.capabilities, plugin.granted(cap) what was granted nothing plugin.data_dir its own folder (TANDEM_PLUGIN_DATA) nothing plugin.log(...) a line to its log (stderr; stdout is the protocol) nothing

A refusal raises Refused, whose capability names what was missing; any other error from the host raises HostError. A handler may ask the host while it runs: the loop reads on one thread and answers each request on its own, so other calls are not held up meanwhile.

docs.title: The examples
docs.text:
note-webhook contributes the observer hook finished at request.finished (payload meta: the request's id, model, tokens and time) and the tool send_note. Both post JSON to the url setting, with the secret WEBHOOK_TOKEN as the bearer when it is granted and set. It asks for network:hooks.example.com: change that to your webhook's host (and its url default) before you install it, since a sandboxed plugin reaches only the hosts it was granted.

keyword-router contributes the provider rules for classify and judge. Its rules setting is a list of {question, label, words}; the first rule of the question whose word the text holds names the label, when the question offers that label, else it answers the first option with confidence 0. It asks for prompts:redacted (the text after the conductor's redaction) and settings:read, and reads its rules from the host at each question when that is granted. To have it answer, add a decision provider of kind plugin with target keyword-router/rules (decision providers).

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: tests/test_plugin_sdk.py installs both examples and a scaffold of each kind, starts them through the plugin host (sandboxed, with the tests' stand-in runtime, and at trust host) and calls them: the webhook is a server on the test machine, so no example needs the network. It also checks the SDK's refusals against the install's, the examples' copies of the SDK against sdk/python, the engine-stats manifests through the installer, and this page's links. The box harness runs it with the rest of the suite; .github/workflows/tests.yml runs it as its own job, by hand.

docs.title: Plugins
docs.text:
A plugin is a folder with a manifest, plugin.json, and a program that speaks MCP over stdio. It can add tools, hooks, decision providers, backends, page panels, skills and in-engine hooks. TandemApp installs it from a folder, a wheel or a git commit, checks it, records the sha256 of its files, and keeps its settings, secrets and granted capabilities.

The contract is contracts/plugin-v1.

Once enabled, the plugin host runs it as one process and wires in what it contributes while it runs (running plugins).

docs.title: Write one
docs.text:
The smallest plugin is examples/hello-tool: one MCP tool that greets a name.

hello-tool/
  plugin.json     the manifest
  server.py       an MCP server over stdio, the standard library only

{
 "plugin_api": "1.0",
 "name": "hello-tool",
 "version": "0.1.0",
 "tandemapp": ">=0.15",
 "hooks_api": "1.0",
 "entry": {"command": ["python3", "server.py"]},
 "contributes": {
  "tools": [{
   "name": "greet",
   "description": "Say hello to someone by name.",
   "inputSchema": {"type": "object", "properties": {"name": {"type": "string"}},
                   "required": ["name"], "additionalProperties": false},
   "annotations": {"readOnlyHint": true, "destructiveHint": false,
                   "idempotentHint": true, "openWorldHint": false}
  }]
 },
 "settings": {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": false,
              "properties": {"greeting": {"type": "string", "default": "Hello"}}}
}

In Python, the plugin SDK writes this reader for you: a plugin is a few decorated functions, and tandemapp-plugin new starts one.

Check it the way an install does, without installing it:

python tools/plugin_check.py path/to/hello-tool
ok hello-tool 0.1.0 sha256 7c51... (2 files)

Two more examples: audit-hook (an observer hook at request.finished) and classify-provider (a decision provider for classify, with a secret and a network host).

docs.title: The manifest
docs.text:
Every field not listed here is refused, not ignored.

field what plugin_api the plugin-v1 version the manifest is written for, 1.0 name the plugin's id: lowercase letters, digits and dashes, at most 48. One plugin of a name. version MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, with an optional -pre kind plugin (default): a program the plugin host runs. engine-stats: a package an engine loads to send its figures; recorded only. title, description, author, license, homepage for the page tandemapp the TandemApp versions it runs on, e.g. >=0.15, <0.17 (>=, >, <=, <, ==, !=, ~=, ==0.16.*) hooks_api the hooks-v1 version it speaks (kind plugin) entry {command: [argv...], env?: {NAME: value}}: started from the manifest's folder, never through a shell (kind plugin) trust sandboxed (default), host or engine: where it asks to run contributes hooks, tools, decision_providers, backends, panels, skills, engine_hooks (below) settings a JSON schema of type object: the plugin's settings, drawn as a form secrets [{name, description?}], names like API_KEY capabilities what it asks for (below) engine_stats kind engine-stats: {engine, package, entry_points, install?, env?} git {submodules: "ignore"}, {lfs: "ignore"}: see git sources

docs.title: Contributions
docs.text: key each item tools an MCP tool: name, description, inputSchema, annotations, optional title and outputSchema hooks name, stages (hooks-v1 stages), role (transform, guard, decider, observer: one the stage takes), payload (meta by default) decision_providers name, questions (the conductor's: classify, packages, deliverable, memory_intent, memory_gate, judge) backends name, description, models panels name, title, path: an HTML file in the plugin, shown in a sandboxed frame skills folders in the plugin, each holding <skill>/SKILL.md; each becomes one more skill folder engine_hooks name, wheel (a .whl in the plugin), hooks (the engine extension's: plan, prompt, at_request, at_block, at_tool_call, check_answer, at_finish, extras, follow_ups, finish); needs trust: engine

docs.title: Tools: the four annotations and strict input
docs.text: Every tool states all four MCP annotations as booleans: readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint and openWorldHint. Its inputSchema is of type object and says "additionalProperties": false on every object in it, nested ones and array items included. A tool that misses one annotation, or a schema that allows extra properties (missing, true, a schema, patternProperties), is refused at install, naming the tool and the annotation or the place in the schema.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
The settings schema is drawn as a form (one generator for plugins, hooks and the conductor's documents: proxy/schemaform.py, and dashboard/src/lib/schema-form.ts for the page). To keep the form and the checks honest it must:

  • be of type object, and say "additionalProperties": false on every object;
  • use only the keywords a form reads: type, properties, required, items, enum, const, anyOf/oneOf (a nullable value, or a list of constants), local $ref to $defs, title, description, default, examples, readOnly, format, pattern, minLength, maxLength, minimum, maximum, exclusiveMinimum, exclusiveMaximum, multipleOf, minItems, maxItems, uniqueItems, minProperties, maxProperties;
  • have defaults that hold against their own schema;
  • nest at most 4 levels and hold at most 200 fields;
  • hold no secret: a secret is a name in secrets, sealed apart and never shown again.

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text:
A plugin gets nothing by default. It asks in capabilities; the admin grants each one in the settings interface. Granted is always a part of what was asked.

capability means grant prompts:meta a hook or provider sees ids, model, sizes, counts, timings, class and tool names pairing's rights prompts:redacted as meta, plus the content after the conductor's redaction pairing's rights prompts:full prompts and answers as they are pairing's rights and a second confirm network:<host>[:<port>] it may connect to this host (a DNS name or an IPv4 address) pairing's rights; a second confirm outside the LAN settings:read it may read the settings interface's values (never a secret) pairing's rights engine:control it may restart the engine or change its mode through the controller pairing's rights and a second confirm secrets:<NAME> the declared secret NAME is passed to its process pairing's rights

A contributed hook's payload needs a prompts: capability at that level or above; a decision provider needs one. Whatever it asks for, a plugin never reads the config database, another plugin's secrets, pairing keys or backend keys.

The plugin host checks each capability where it is used, and a refusal is journaled: in the plugin's status (refusals) and in the audit table (refused, by plugin:<id>, the capability's name, never a value).

capability checked where prompts:<level> a hook's payload when it is registered and at each call; a decision provider's input network:<host>[:<port>] the sandbox's egress filter: only these hosts settings:read tandem/settings and the panel bridge's settings.read secrets:<NAME> the process's environment and tandem/secret engine:control refused, whatever is granted, until engine control for plugins exists

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
POST /v1/fleet/plugins {"source": {"type": "folder", "path": "/srv/plugins/hello-tool"}}
POST /v1/fleet/plugins {"source": {"type": "wheel", "path": "/srv/hello_tool-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl"}}
POST /v1/fleet/plugins {"source": {"type": "git", "url": "https://example.com/hello.git",
                                   "commit": "<40 hex digits>", "subdir": "plugins/hello"}}

POST /v1/fleet/plugins/inspect with the same source runs every check and installs nothing.

A wheel that is not on the controller's disk can be sent to it: POST /v1/fleet/plugins/upload?name=hello_tool-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl with the wheel's bytes as the body (Content-Type: application/octet-stream, at most 32 MiB, pairing's rights). The controller keeps it in its plugins' upload folder for an hour and answers the source to inspect and install it with; after that it is removed.

GET /v1/fleet/plugins carries each plugin's run state from the plugin host (run: its state, restarts, last error and gave_up), so a list needs no status call per plugin. Every plugin's view names the requested capabilities whose grant takes the second confirm (capabilities.confirm), as inspect does. Every time in the API is in milliseconds since the epoch.

Nothing in a plugin runs at install. A folder is copied file by file. A wheel is read as a zip, never through pip: its manifest is at its root or in one top-level folder, every member stays inside the tree, no member is a symlink, and the hashes in its RECORD must hold. A git source is fetched into an empty repository with no system or user git config, no hooks and no prompt, over https, ssh or file only, and its files are read out of the commit one blob at a time: no checkout, so no filter, attribute or LFS smudge runs.

A git source is pinned to a commit: the full id (40 hex digits). A branch name, a tag name or a short id is refused, because each can move. A submodule or an LFS file refuses the install, since its content is not in the commit, unless the manifest says "git": {"submodules": "ignore"} or {"lfs": "ignore"}: then the submodule's folder stays empty and an LFS file stays a pointer.

The checks, each a refusal with its code and the manifest field it is about (contracts/plugin-v1/api.json checks lists them all):

  • the manifest parses, fits the schema and its kind's rules;
  • the tools' annotations and strict input schemas;
  • unique names within each contribution; hooks at real stages with a role the stage takes; providers for real questions;
  • paths that stay in the plugin and exist;
  • secrets:<NAME> names a declared secret; payloads covered by a prompts: capability; engine_hooks only with trust: engine;
  • the settings schema, as above;
  • tandemapp holds for this TandemApp, hooks_api and plugin_api are not newer than this controller's (same major, minor not newer). A refusal names the needed version and this one's;
  • a signature, when there is one, holds;
  • with the policy on, a sandboxed plugin carries a trusted signature (409 signature_required).

docs.title: The tree's sha256 and a signature
docs.text:
The install records the sha256 of the plugin's files: sha256 over plugin-tree-v1\n and a line a file, in byte order of the path, <sha256 of the file> <x or -> <path>\n (x: executable). .git and __pycache__ folders, .pyc, .DS_Store and ._* files are not part of the tree; a symlink or a special file refuses it. The registry checks the tree again when the plugin is enabled and before it is started, and plugin.sig.json with it (the tree's sha256 leaves the signature out, so the registry records the signature file's own sha256): a tree or a signature that changed reads mismatch (or missing), with the reason, and does not load until it is installed again. The health page names it (plugin_tampered).

A plugin may carry a signature, plugin.sig.json at its root (signing). When it is present it must hold, or the install is refused (signature_invalid).

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
install the plugin is stored under the controller's state dir, plugins/<name>/<version>/, disabled enable checks the tree and the compatibility with this TandemApp first disable always works upgrade install the new version with "upgrade": true. Settings whose property is still there and whose value still holds, secrets still declared and capabilities still asked for are kept; the rest is dropped and listed. A new capability starts ungranted (listed in new): it takes its own grant. The old version's folder is removed. The same version with other files is refused (raise the version); an older version needs "allow_downgrade": true, signed or not. A version that asks a higher trust level, or whose host grant rested on a signature it no longer carries, is refused (409 trust_confirm_needed) and the installed version keeps running, until it comes again with "confirm_trust": "<plugin id>" (trust). remove refused while a hook names the plugin (409 referenced, with the hooks); takes its folder and secrets

An install cut short leaves nothing: the files move into place before the registry row is written, and the next start removes a staging folder or a version folder no row names.

docs.title: Sign a plugin
docs.text:
tools/plugin_sign.py makes an ed25519 key and signs a plugin folder with it; it never prints the private key.

python tools/plugin_sign.py keygen ~/keys/acme-plugins.pem      # 0600, never overwritten
public_key g2KYlmjw...UZJzY=
fingerprint sha256:27b251a6f466ff65ffa8c9f9dc4a3033d3752871cc05faea0637f08152a37788

python tools/plugin_sign.py sign --key ~/keys/acme-plugins.pem path/to/hello-tool
python tools/plugin_sign.py verify path/to/hello-tool --fingerprint sha256:27b2...7788

--passphrase-env NAME encrypts the key at keygen and reads the passphrase at sign. Publish the public key and its fingerprint where your users can compare them. Sign last: a file changed after signing breaks the signature.

What is signed. plugin.sig.json holds {format, algorithm, public_key, plugin, version, tree_sha256, manifest_sha256, signature}: format is tandemapp-plugin-sig-1, algorithm ed25519, public_key the base64 of the key's 32 bytes, tree_sha256 the tree's sha256 (above: it folds in every file's sha256) and manifest_sha256 the sha256 of plugin.json's bytes. signature is the base64 of the 64-byte ed25519 signature over five lines of UTF-8, each ending in \n:

tandemapp-plugin-sig-1
plugin <name>
version <version>
tree <tree_sha256>
manifest <manifest_sha256>

The install checks each part: the tree, the manifest, the name and the version must be this plugin's, and the signature must hold. A key's id is the first 16 hex digits of its fingerprint, the sha256 of its 32 bytes.

docs.title: Trust
docs.text:
A signature that holds is only trusted when its key is one this TandemApp trusts for that plugin at that level. A signature by any other key counts as none.

A route that takes pairing's rights (install, upload, enable, remove, a trust grant, the keys and the policy) answers 403 trust_required to a caller that may change the configuration but has not those rights (with no admin password set: any other machine), and 401 to one that may not change the configuration at all.

Trusted keys (/v1/fleet/plugin-trust, pairing's rights to change). Adding a key takes its fingerprint typed or pasted back: compare it with the one its publisher published. Without it the answer is 428 fingerprint_confirm_required with the fingerprint to compare; a different one is 422 fingerprint_mismatch. A key can be limited to plugin ids (plugins) and to trust levels (levels); null means any. Removing a key takes its fingerprint as well. To change a key's limits, remove it and add it again.

POST /v1/fleet/plugin-trust/keys {"public_key": "g2KYlmjw...UZJzY=", "name": "Acme plugins",
                                  "plugins": ["hello-tool"], "levels": ["sandboxed", "host"],
                                  "confirm_fingerprint": "sha256:27b251a6...7788"}
DELETE /v1/fleet/plugin-trust/keys/27b251a6f466ff65 {"confirm_fingerprint": "sha256:27b2...7788"}
POST /v1/fleet/plugin-trust/policy {"require_signature_sandboxed": true}

The levels.

level runs when a grant takes sandboxed always; with require_signature_sandboxed on (off by default), only with a trusted signature, refused at install, enable and load otherwise nothing host it holds a host grant pairing's rights, and either a signature trusted for host (basis signature) or the plugin's id typed (basis typed). A grant on a signature holds only while that signature stays trusted: remove the key, and the plugin stops until it is granted again engine not yet: the in-process chain does not exist per engine host: a signature trusted for engine AND the plugin's id typed. The grant is recorded; the plugin is refused at runtime until engine extensions install through ext install 
GET  /v1/fleet/plugins/<id>/trust                      what it asks, what it has, its signature,
                                                       whether it runs and what a grant takes
POST /v1/fleet/plugins/<id>/trust {"level": "host", "confirm": "<id>"}
POST /v1/fleet/plugins/<id>/trust {"level": "engine", "engine": "<engine host>", "confirm": "<id>"}
POST /v1/fleet/plugins/<id>/trust {"level": "sandboxed"}                     revoke every grant
POST /v1/fleet/plugins/<id>/trust {"level": "sandboxed", "engine": "<host>"}  revoke one engine

A grant without the typed confirmation where one is needed is 428 typed_confirm_required; a wrong one is 422 typed_confirm_mismatch; an engine grant without a trusted signature is 409 signature_required. The settings interface's trust key grants host only for a plugin signed by a key trusted for host (with its second confirm); for an unsigned one it answers 409 and points here.

Updates. A new capability starts ungranted. A version that asks a higher level than the installed one, or whose host grant rested on a signature this version does not carry, waits for confirm_trust (the plugin's id): the installed version keeps running meanwhile. With it, the upgrade goes ahead, and a host plugin's grant is renewed on the new version's trusted signature or, unsigned, on the typed confirmation. A host grant carries over an upgrade that still asks host; an engine grant carries over while the new version is still signed by a key trusted for engine. Going back to an older version, signed or not, takes allow_downgrade.

Audit. Each trust decision is a row of the audit table: a key trusted or distrusted (with its fingerprint), the policy set, a grant or revoke (its level, basis, key and engine host), and each refusal at install, upgrade, enable, load or grant (refused, with where and why). The health page names a plugin that may not run as it asks (plugin_untrusted) or that changed (plugin_tampered).

docs.title: Running plugins
docs.text: The plugin host in the controller starts one process for each enabled plugin of kind plugin, from entry.command (argv, never a shell) in the manifest's folder. It reads the registry every 2 seconds and at each change: a disabled or removed plugin stops, a plugin whose settings, secrets, grants or version changed starts again with them.

docs.title: Trust levels
docs.text:
trust where it runs how sandboxed (default) a container (Docker or Podman) or a Kubernetes pod of the chat sandbox's class always, signed or not, unless the policy requires a trusted signature for sandboxed plugins; it waits when there is no sandbox runtime here host a process of the app's user, outside any sandbox only once granted (trust): on a signature by a trusted key, or with the plugin's id typed; until then it does not start engine a wheel inside the engine a grant per engine host takes a trusted signature and the plugin's id typed; refused at runtime until the in-process chain exists

The sandbox. The sandbox image (QSE_SANDBOX_IMAGE, tandem-sandbox:1), uid 1000, every capability dropped, no-new-privileges, a read-only root, a small in-memory /tmp, no devices, 512 MiB (TANDEM_PLUGIN_MEM_MB), one CPU and 128 processes, and no network but its loopback. Mounted: the plugin's installed tree at /plugin, read-only; its own folder at /workspace (TANDEM_PLUGIN_DATA) and a home at /home/agent. Nothing else of the controller's: not the config database, not another plugin's folder or secrets. Its way out is the chat sandbox's egress proxy (HTTP_PROXY and HTTPS_PROXY are set) with a host list: only the hosts of its granted network: capabilities, a granted LAN address included; any other address is refused, and this box (loopback), link-local addresses and the Kubernetes API are refused even when granted.

Which runtime. The one chatd uses on this install: QSE_SANDBOX_BACKEND, QSE_SANDBOX_SOCKET and QSE_SANDBOX_IMAGE from the controller's environment or chatd's env file (<state dir>/chatd.env). TANDEM_PLUGIN_SANDBOX (auto, docker, kubernetes, off) overrides it. In a cluster a plugin's pod is made like a chat's sandbox pod, its tree a read-only subPath of the release's volume, and reaches only the plugin host's egress port (sandbox.kubernetes.pluginEgressPort, 3129, TANDEM_PLUGIN_EGRESS_PORT). With no runtime a sandboxed plugin does not start: its state is unavailable and the health page says why (plugin_no_sandbox).

The environment holds only what the grants allow, never the controller's:

variable what TANDEM_PLUGIN, TANDEM_PLUGIN_VERSION its id and version TANDEM_PLUGIN_SETTINGS its own settings as JSON, each schema default filled in TANDEM_PLUGIN_DATA its own data folder TANDEM_PLUGIN_CAPABILITIES the capabilities granted, a JSON list <NAME> each secret granted by secrets:<NAME> (a name the process itself uses, such as PATH or HOME, is not passed) entry.env, LANG, PYTHONUNBUFFERED the manifest's own values and two defaults

A host plugin also gets this process's PATH, and its data folder as HOME.

docs.title: Supervision
docs.text: A plugin that exits, or does not answer initialize within 20 seconds, is started again after 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, then 60 seconds. At the fifth failure within an hour the host gives up: it disables the plugin (audited, by plugin-host) and the health page names it (plugin_failed) until it is enabled again. A stop by hand holds it until a start by hand. Removing a running plugin ends its process before its folder goes.

docs.title: The protocol
docs.text:
MCP over stdio, one JSON-RPC 2.0 message a line, protocol revision 2025-06-18: initialize, then tools/list when the manifest declares tools, tools/call, ping. Three more methods carry what MCP has no words for, and the plugin answers those it contributes:

method params answer hooks/call the hooks-v1 envelope (hooks, id, stage, ts, payload, mode, request, event) with hook set to the contributed hook's name and hook_id to the runner's id a hooks-v1 result: {action: continue\|modify\|deny\|decide, patch?, decision?, reason?, labels?} decision/ask {provider, question, instructions, options, model, deadline_ms, payload, input}; input is {chars} at meta, {text} at redacted (after the conductor's redaction) and full {label, confidence?, probabilities?}: label one of options backend/request {backend, method, path, body} {status, body}, or {status, events: [...]} for a stream (each event one SSE data: line)

The plugin may ask the host, with requests of its own on the same stream:

method params needs tandem/settings none settings:read: its own settings tandem/secret {name} secrets:<name>; another plugin's secret never tandem/engine any refused until engine control for plugins exists

A refusal is the JSON-RPC error -32001 with data.capability. The calls are local, so they carry no signature; the payload levels still apply.

docs.title: Contributions
docs.text: Each contribution is registered while the plugin runs and is gone when it stops. A plugin's status says what was registered and what was not, and why (notes).

docs.title: Tools
docs.text: Offered to the Chat tab: chatd lists them with its MCP servers (plugin:<id>, transport plugin, read-only there) as mcp__plugin_<id>__<tool>, and calls them through the controller (/chat-engine/v1/plugins/tools, /chat-engine/v1/plugins/tools/call), so Chat must be on to use them. Only a tool the manifest declares and the server lists is offered, with the manifest's checked schema and annotations; arguments outside the schema are refused before the plugin sees them.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text: Each hook joins the runner as <plugin>/<hook>: priority 100, mode on, no scope, the manifest's stages, role and payload. A hook whose payload is above the plugin's granted prompts: level is not registered. To set its priority, scope, mode or policy, add a hook of kind plugin on the hooks' API with target <plugin>/<hook> (at the declared stages, role and payload or below): it takes the contributed hook's place. The runner's timeouts, breaker and policies apply as for any hook.

docs.title: Decision providers
docs.text: Each provider is registered as <plugin>/<provider> in shadow: asked off the request's path and journaled, never used. To have it answer, add a decision provider of kind plugin with target <plugin>/<provider> and the mode you want (on, ab): it takes the contributed one's place.

docs.title: Backends
docs.text: Each backend becomes a row of the backends store, plugin-<id>-<name> (kind generic, the manifest's models, labelled "(plugin )"), whose URL is this controller's /plugin-backends/<id>/<name>: requests that the gateway routes there go to the plugin as backend/request, GET /v1/models answers the manifest's models. That route answers this machine only. The row is removed when the plugin stops.

docs.title: Skills
docs.text: Each skill folder of a running plugin is one more skill folder of the controller's conductor, after the packages document's own skill_dirs, read from the installed tree (never written).

docs.title: Panels
docs.text:
A panel is served at /plugin-panels/<id>/<panel>/ (its HTML; the files beside it under the same path) with Content-Security-Policy: sandbox allow-scripts allow-forms; default-src 'none'; ...; connect-src 'none': in the page's iframe or on its own it has an opaque origin, so it reads no cookie, storage or route of the controller's. It talks to the page with postMessage({type: 'tandem-bridge', id, method, params}); the page relays the call to POST /v1/fleet/plugins/<id>/bridge and posts back {type: 'tandem-bridge-result', id, result | error}.

bridge method needs plugin.info, plugin.status nothing tools.call {tool, arguments} the tool is the plugin's own and read-only (readOnlyHint) settings.read settings:read engine.control refused: not available yet

GET /v1/fleet/plugins/<id>/panels lists them with the bridge's methods this plugin may use.

docs.title: Write a sandboxed plugin
docs.text:
• Use the standard library, or vendor what you need into the plugin: the sandbox has the image's Python 3.12 and Node, its root is read-only, and its network reaches only the hosts you ask for.
  • Read your settings from TANDEM_PLUGIN_SETTINGS; keep files in TANDEM_PLUGIN_DATA.
  • Ask for network:<host>[:<port>] for each host you call; HTTP clients that honour HTTPS_PROXY (urllib, requests, curl) go through the proxy as they are.
  • Write logs to stderr; stdout is the protocol.
  • examples/hello-tool, audit-hook and classify-provider are complete plugins written against the protocol itself; note-webhook and keyword-router are built on the SDK. The tests run each of them.

docs.title: Debugging
docs.text: what where running or why not, restarts, the last error, what was registered, the refusals GET /v1/fleet/plugins/<id>/status its stderr and the host's lines about it, every secret value replaced by [secret NAME] GET /v1/fleet/plugins/<id>/logs?tail=200; <state dir>/logs/plugins/<id>.log (1 MiB, then one older file) start again, stop (held), start POST /v1/fleet/plugins/<id>/restart, /stop, /start a hook's calls and breaker GET /v1/fleet/hooks/<id>/calls for a hook of kind plugin; the runner's metrics for <plugin>/<hook> a plugin that gave up, has no sandbox, changed since its install or is not trusted as it asks the health page's controller findings why it may not run at its level GET /v1/fleet/plugins/<id>/trust

docs.title: The API
docs.text:
route rights GET /v1/fleet/plugins the configuration's POST /v1/fleet/plugins/inspect {source} the configuration's POST /v1/fleet/plugins {source, upgrade?, allow_downgrade?, confirm_trust?} pairing's POST /v1/fleet/plugins/upload?name=<file>.whl (the wheel's bytes) pairing's GET /v1/fleet/plugins/{id} the configuration's GET /v1/fleet/plugins/{id}/trust the configuration's POST /v1/fleet/plugins/{id}/trust {level, engine?, confirm?} pairing's GET /v1/fleet/plugin-trust the configuration's POST /v1/fleet/plugin-trust/keys, DELETE /v1/fleet/plugin-trust/keys/{key}, POST /v1/fleet/plugin-trust/policy pairing's POST /v1/fleet/plugins/{id}/enable pairing's POST /v1/fleet/plugins/{id}/disable, /verify the configuration's DELETE /v1/fleet/plugins/{id} pairing's GET /v1/fleet/plugins/{id}/status, /logs, /panels the configuration's POST /v1/fleet/plugins/{id}/start, /stop, /restart, /bridge the configuration's

Pairing's rights are the admin's, or this machine's while no admin password is set. No answer holds a secret. Starting a plugin takes it enabled first, which takes pairing's rights.

docs.title: Settings, secrets and capabilities
docs.text: They are the settings interface's plugins scope, one target a plugin: GET /v1/settings/plugins/schema?target=<id>, then plan and apply as for any scope (settings). Its keys are enabled, settings.<property>, secrets.<NAME> (write-only), capabilities.<capability> and, for a manifest that asks trust: host, trust (host only on a trusted signature; trust). Each plugin keeps its own versions.

docs.title: The Plugins pages
docs.text:
The dashboard has all of this under Settings, Plugins.

  • The list. Each installed plugin with its version, its kind, where it came from, its trust level, its signature and its state. The state is the run state the list carries; no plugin is asked alone.
  • Install. A folder or a wheel on the controller's machine, a wheel uploaded from this computer, or a git URL with a full commit id. The source is checked first. The page then shows every check with how it ended, the sha256 of the files, where the plugin asks to run, each capability in plain words with its risk, and what it adds. Install comes after that. A refused source installs nothing; each reason stands with what to change and the controller's own sentence.
  • A plugin's page. Its state, restarts and last error, with start, stop and restart; what it adds and where each shows; its settings as a form drawn from its schema; its secrets, set or removed and never shown; each capability with its grant; its log; its files, with a check against the sha256 of the install; a newer version; and its removal. A plugin that is off has one button that stages the switch and everything it asks for.
  • A panel. The plugin's own page in a sandboxed frame. The page relays the frame's bridge calls to /v1/fleet/plugins/<id>/bridge, only the methods GET .../panels lists for it; anything else is refused on the page. A panel that cannot be shown says why.

The switch, the settings, the secrets, the grants and the trust level are staged and go through the settings' review, which asks a second time for prompts:full, engine:control, a network host outside the LAN and the host. Install, upgrade, removal, start, stop and restart are done at once.

A wheel is named by its path on the controller's machine, or uploaded from the browser's computer through POST /v1/fleet/plugins/upload: the page then checks it from the path the controller answers, which holds for an hour. Which grants ask a second time is the controller's word (capabilities.confirm); the page reads a host itself only for a controller that does not say.

docs.title: The engine-stats plugins
docs.text: The two packages in plugins/ that an engine loads to send its figures have a manifest of kind engine-stats. The controller can check and record them; installing them into the engine stays pip install plugins/<engine>.

docs.title: The proxy: one dashboard in front of any OpenAI-compatible backend
docs.text:
The dashboard can sit in front of other engines and cloud APIs, not only this one. Clients send their OpenAI requests to one address; the proxy routes each request by its model id to the backend that serves it and copies the answer back byte for byte. On the way it records what a client could measure: tokens from usage, time to first token, decode tokens a second, cached and reasoning tokens when the provider reports them, and the cost at the model's price. One ledger and one dashboard cover every backend.

Backends in this release:

kind what it is routes relayed tandemllm another TandemLLM server, by URL chat, completions, embeddings, Responses generic vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, LM Studio, Ollama, any OpenAI-compatible server chat, completions, embeddings, Responses openai OpenAI's API with your key chat, completions, embeddings, Responses deepseek DeepSeek's API with your key chat, completions anthropic any Anthropic-compatible (Messages API) server, by base URL, with your key chat, translated

Every backend also answers clients of the Messages API, through /v1/messages (see "The Messages API" below).

The proxy only observes in this release. It never changes a request's meaning: it sets the model id the backend knows, and it asks a stream for its usage frame when the client did not (then it drops that frame before the client). The conductor's features (task class, effort, packages, the loop and tool checks) come to foreign backends in a later release. Their switches are already stored per model.

A backend of kind anthropic (SRV-877) is the one kind whose bytes are not copied: an OpenAI chat completion is translated to a Messages request (<base>/v1/messages, the base URL with or without /v1) and the answer, its stream and its errors back to OpenAI's shape, before the ledger, the hooks and the client read them. The key goes as x-api-key (or a bearer, anthropic.auth) with anthropic-version (anthropic.api_version, 2023-06-01 by default); none of the client's headers goes on. What has no equal is refused with a 400 that names the field (n above 1, response_format json_object, audio and file parts, tools other than functions, tool arguments that are not JSON). temperature, top_p and top_k are dropped unless anthropic.sampling is pass; presence_penalty, frequency_penalty, logit_bias, seed, logprobs, top_logprobs and user are dropped too, and the answer's X-Tandem-Dropped header names each one the client sent. max_tokens is the client's, else anthropic.default_max_tokens (16,000; 64,000 for a stream; capped by the model's limit). reasoning_effort asks for thinking (anthropic.thinking_shape: adaptive with output_config.effort, budget, or off); thinking text comes back as reasoning_content, without its signature (the thinking stash below sends the earlier turns' blocks back upstream with theirs). With anthropic.auto_cache on (the default) a request carries one top-level cache breakpoint. A 529 is tried again like a 429 or 503, and reaches an OpenAI client as 503. Not passed on: redacted thinking, server-tool blocks, citations, the stop string that matched, and stream events the translation does not know. The model list is read page by page (after_id). Variables: TANDEM_BACKEND_<ID>_ANTHROPIC_AUTH, _ANTHROPIC_API_VERSION, _ANTHROPIC_SAMPLING, _ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS, _ANTHROPIC_AUTO_CACHE, _ANTHROPIC_THINKING_DISPLAY, _ANTHROPIC_THINKING_SHAPE.

docs.title: The Messages API
docs.text:
Clients that speak the Messages API use TandemApp too (SRV-879): POST /v1/messages, whole or streamed, and POST /v1/messages/count_tokens, with the same keys as the OpenAI routes, sent as x-api-key or as Authorization: Bearer. Neither goes on to a backend. With TANDEM_AUTH=accounts the key is an API token with the scope inference:anthropic (and its model list, 403 permission_error naming the model), and every refusal of the sign-in on these routes is in the Messages API's shape too; the ledger row's api column says anthropic. On a route of Messages API backends the request passes through (below); on any other route anthropic-version (accepted, never required) and anthropic-beta do not go on either, and the request is translated to a chat completion and runs the pipeline every chat completion runs (the routes, the deployments, the hooks, the harness, the ledger, whose row says messages), and the answer comes back in the Messages API's shape: content blocks, a stop reason, usage, and errors as {type: "error", error: {type, message}, request_id} with a request-id header on every answer. A drained node or a full backend is 529 overloaded_error with its Retry-After. A stream sends message_start, each block's start, deltas and stop, message_delta with the counts, then message_stop; while nothing has gone out for 15 seconds (a long prefill, a queue) it sends ping.

What it costs. A system prompt's blocks become one system message (their boundaries are lost). Every cache_control is dropped (a local engine caches prefixes by itself): cache_read_input_tokens is the backend's cached count, cache_creation_input_tokens 0, input_tokens the rest. thinking and output_config.effort become the backend's own switch; budget_tokens is not a hard cap there. Reasoning comes back as a thinking block with a signature TandemApp makes; sent back, those blocks are dropped from the history, as are redacted and foreign ones. A tool result's images and its is_error are lost (its text stays). metadata never goes on. top_k reaches a local engine only. The stop string that matched is named only where the backend names it. Each tool call's input arrives as one input_json_delta when the call is whole. Refused with a 400 that names it: server tools and other tool types without a schema, document and other block types the chat shape has no place for, mcp_servers, container. Every field the request goes without is named in X-Tandem-Dropped.

count_tokens is exact or a 404 not_found_error, never an estimate: a TandemLLM engine (a local backend that answers its tokenize route) counts with that route (the model's chat template over the translated request), a backend of kind anthropic with its own count_tokens; other backends answer 404. A route that mixes a backend of kind anthropic with backends of other kinds (a fallback of another kind) is translated, twice on the anthropic backend (to the chat shape, then to the Messages API again), so it loses what both translations lose. /v1/messages/batches answers 404.

docs.title: Pass-through
docs.text:
When every backend of a model's route (the backend and its fallbacks) is of kind anthropic, a Messages API request passes through (SRV-881): nothing is translated and nothing is lost. The body goes upstream as the client sent it, byte for byte, with two exceptions: the client's key is replaced by the backend's (x-api-key, or a bearer with anthropic.auth), and the model value is set to the upstream id when the model has a public id of its own (only that value changes; key order, spacing and escapes stay, so the cache prefix holds). Of the client's headers only content-type, anthropic-version (the backend's anthropic.api_version when the client sends none) and anthropic-beta go on. The answer, its stream (thinking blocks, signatures, events this server does not know) and the backend's own errors come back as the backend sent them, with its request-id. count_tokens passes through the same way. The ledger reads the usage, the stop reason and the tool calls beside the bytes; its row says messages. Answers of TandemApp's own (a drained node, a timeout, a hook's refusal) are in the Messages API's error shape; a stream that breaks ends with an error event.

With no hook enabled no translation code runs. With hooks, every stage sees a canonical copy in the chat shape and request.protocol says {inbound: messages, upstream: messages} (hooks-v1 1.1, docs/hooks.md). Guards, deciders and observers work as for any request. A transform's patch of a parameter that has a Messages API field (model, max_tokens, temperature, top_p, top_k, stop, metadata, tool_choice, parallel_tool_calls, reasoning_effort, response_format json_schema) is written into the request; a patch of the messages, the tools, the answer or a parameter without such a field is not applied: it is journaled refused with protocol_native and the hook's failure policy applies (closed: 503 hook_unavailable, which a Messages API client reads as 529). A hook that moves the request to a backend of another kind (a new model, route.select) refuses it (409 protocol_native); a request.error fallback of another kind is not tried, and the backend's own failure goes to the client. The harness never runs on these requests.

docs.title: The thinking stash
docs.text:
An OpenAI-shaped client has no place for a thinking block's signature, so in a tool loop on a backend of kind anthropic it sends the earlier assistant turns back as text and tool calls only, and a server that checks thinking against the conversation refuses such a history or answers without the reasoning. TandemApp keeps each translated answer's own content blocks (thinking, its signature, redacted thinking, text, tool calls) in memory and, when the client sends that turn back, sends them upstream in place of the translated ones (SRV-881). A turn is found by the client's key (a hash; another key never reads it; with TANDEM_AUTH=accounts the API token's id, so a rotated token keeps its turns, or the signed-in account's), the backend, the upstream model (blocks never go to another backend or model) and the turn's tool call ids (a turn without calls: its place in the history and its text). Bounds: 64 MB and 1 hour since a turn was last kept or sent, least recently used out first. A turn the stash evicted goes without its thinking, and so does every earlier turn (thinking may be missing from the front of a history, not from its middle); the answer's X-Tandem-Dropped names thinking and the ledger row's error_type says thinking_evicted. A turn whose tool calls the client changed is not restored. The stash is lost when TandemApp restarts.

The harness does not run on a backend of kind anthropic (SRV-879): its own requests (the class question, the narrator, the memory writer) speak the OpenAI chat shape, and translated they would lose the log probabilities, the greedy sampling and the thinking switch they rely on. The backend's harness mode and writer cannot be switched on there (a 422 naming the field, or an error naming the variable), a role whose endpoint names such a backend is not asked, and the health page says harness_unsupported while anything still asks for it.

docs.title: On its own
docs.text:
Anyone without a GPU runs the same code as TandemApp, the tandem-app command. It needs Python 3.11 or newer, the standard library and cryptography, and never pulls torch. A checkout has no built page (see "The built page" below), so build it first, with Node 20.19 or newer, or fetch a released one:

python3 tools/dashboard_bundle.py build     # npm ci and npm run build in dashboard/
pip install .                       # or '.[host]': adds psutil and NVML for the System view
tandem-app                          # 127.0.0.1:8080, ~/.tandemllm/config.sqlite3
open http://127.0.0.1:8080/dashboard/

python -m proxy in the checkout does the same without installing anything but cryptography. The page opens on Setup while no backend exists. The engine-only panels (caches, speculation, the conductor, memory) say that this server has no engine.

From a DeepSeek key to a row in the Usage view takes five commands:

pip install '.[host]'
printf 'TANDEM_BACKENDS=deepseek\nTANDEM_BACKEND_DEEPSEEK_KIND=deepseek\nTANDEM_BACKEND_DEEPSEEK_KEY=%s\n' "$DEEPSEEK_API_KEY" > app.env && chmod 600 app.env
tandem-app check --env-file app.env
tandem-app serve --env-file app.env &
curl -s localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"deepseek-chat","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hi"}]}'

Then open http://127.0.0.1:8080/dashboard/#/usage.

docs.title: In one command
docs.text:
A release archive carries the built page, so a host installs TandemApp with its Python 3.11 or newer alone (OPS-282; Linux on arm64 or x86_64, or macOS): no Node, no git, no root.

tar -xzf tandemapp-<version>.tar.gz && bash tandemapp-<version>/packaging/install.sh

packaging/install.sh (packaging/tandemapp_install.py) copies the release to ~/.local/share/tandemapp/releases/<version>-<hash>, makes one venv for it with this host's Python and the app extra (cryptography, psutil), writes the state dir ~/.tandemllm (mode 0700) with a fresh master key (secrets.key) and app.env (127.0.0.1:8080, Chat off, no conductor, no TandemNode agent: a bare TandemApp, OPS-288), points ~/.local/share/tandemapp/current at the release and starts it: a systemd user unit tandem-app on Linux (packaging/linux's unit and launcher), a launchd job org.tandemllm.app on macOS, a background process where no service manager answers (a container). It waits for /health to name this release and its page, then prints the URL; the first page is the setup wizard (GET /v1/fleet/app's setup.needs_setup).
