On four recorded opencode sessions the 2B wrote a phrase in 308 to 369 ms at the median, in slices of at most 150 ms (measured, tools/voice_replay.py).

docs.title: The shadow reader
docs.text:
A small Qwen3.5 model keeps its own state of each coding session: its KV rows and its Gated DeltaNet state for every token the session holds, the served prompt and the model's output. It reads each turn's new tokens and nothing else, so a small model can answer a question about a 100,000-token session in one forward of the question. It is off until QWEN38_SHADOW_MODEL names a model (qwen3.5-0.8b).

Two cheaper ways to give a small model the big model's context were tried first and failed: a few soft tokens made from the 27B's hidden rows answered at chance, and a per-layer map from the 27B's state into a small model's reached a held-out R² of about 0.5, far from what agreement needs. The small model's own state of the same tokens is exact, and that is what the shadow keeps.

Exact on a grid. The state advances only in whole chunks of 512 rows at absolute positions k · 512. A fresh prefill of the same ids on the same grid runs the same chunks on the same inputs, so the two states are equal bit for bit, however many turns it took. Measured on the GPU on two real conversations of 41,802 and 58,278 tokens: every KV row, the recurrent state and the convolution state equal a fresh prefill on the same grid (measured, the 0.4.0 series). When a new prompt differs from what was read (a template drops an earlier turn's reasoning), the reader goes back to the newest checkpoint at or below the difference, one kept at each turn's prompt end.

When it reads. While the big model decodes, only it and its drafters use the GPU. The reader has two windows. In the idle window it looks every 0.2 s, and when no request runs or waits it reads for at most 2 s, checking before every chunk whether a request waits; a request that arrives waits at most one chunk, 36 to 50 ms on the 0.8B. Inside a turn it may use 2 % of the time since the model's first token, in slices between two rounds. The idle window alone is not enough for an agent: in the ledger's opencode sessions the median gap between one request's end and the next one's start is 0.31 s.

What it costs. With the shadow on, the big model's decode on a 16,350-token prompt went from 36.02 to 35.28 tok/s, -2.05 %, and the time to first token did not move (measured, tools/shadow_ab.py, 6 runs an arm, the 0.4.0 series). That is the 2 % share, as designed.

session depth (tokens) 0 16,384 33,000 41,000 Qwen3.5-0.8B, ms per 512-row chunk 36.4 41.1 49.9 Qwen3.5-2B, ms per 512-row chunk 50.5 56.1 69.1

The shadow reader's read rate: milliseconds per 512-row chunk at three depths of the session (the 2B's last point at 33k). Measured: tools/shadow_measure.py with the served process's arithmetic flags, median of 3, the 0.4.0 series.

Who asks.

ask(session, question, choices), also POST /v1/conductor/shadow/ask, is a typed decision of the small model over the whole session: each choice is a letter, and one forward of the question gives the letters' softmax. At the end of a 41k session the router's 9-class question took 68 ms on the 0.8B (measured). In the coding profile the router's class question is asked of the shadow in shadow mode on turns of at least 8,192 tokens and journaled beside the router's own class; nothing of the turn changes.

What that journal showed is a result in its own right. On 58 journaled turns, the small models agreed with the router's class no better than a constant answer does:

model classes with descriptions short labels only Qwen3.5-0.8B 8 of 58 2 of 58 Qwen3.5-2B 25 of 58 8 of 58 Qwen3.5-4B 19 of 58 44 of 58

The router's question asked of the shadow on 58 journaled turns of 6 opencode sessions. A constant code_edit scores 42 of 58. (measured), tools/shadow_router_eval.py, 2026-10-05.

The shadow therefore keeps the 0.8B (1.5 GiB of weights, the fastest read) and the question stays in shadow. A question the small models can answer, such as two or three coarse classes asked only where the router decides fresh, is the next thing to try.

Memory. Resident states are capped at QWEN38_SHADOW_GB (4 GiB). Past the cap, the least recently used session goes to the NVMe (QWEN38_SHADOW_DISK, one file a session, 48 h) and comes back exact. A 58k session is 0.88 GiB on the 0.8B. The model loads through the residency planner in an idle window soon after the start, and its own pool, up to its claim, is left out of the engine's memory ceiling. A live memory pool never gives its free segments back, so after an idle burst that leaves more than QWEN38_SHADOW_POOL_SLACK_GIB (2) free in the pool, the shadow parks its sessions on the disk and unloads the model; the next turn loads it again and reads on from the disk.

docs.title: Threat model
docs.text: This page is for security researchers and for reviewers of a change. It says where untrusted input enters TandemApp and which parts matter most. The engine has its own page, the engine's threat model, which also says how to report.

docs.title: What runs and where input enters
docs.text:
TandemApp runs on one machine on a home or office LAN, in front of one or more engines. It has five parts:

part what it does code controller (tandem-app), port 8080 the dashboard's page and API, the OpenAI API in front of other OpenAI-compatible backends and cloud APIs, the fleet, the usage ledger proxy/, tandemapp/ chatd, 127.0.0.1:8016 the Chat tab (beta): conversations, agent runs, tools, MCP, uploads; the engine (in chat mode) and the controller forward /v1/chat-app/* to it chatd/, tandemapp/chat_forward.py chat sandbox one Docker or Podman container per chat, --network none; its only way out is chatd's egress proxy chatd/sandbox.py, chatd/egress.py dashboard the web UI, served by the controller, and by an engine in chat mode while the engine still carries TandemApp dashboard/ TandemNode, 7700 the agent the controller reads a node through; mTLS with pinned certificates after pairing, a pairing window on 7701 while a code is shown proxy/nodeagent.py, proxy/pairing.py

Every route of the controller but /health, the page shell and the sign-in needs an account's session or an API token (auth.md). Until the first owner exists, only the one-time setup code opens the first-run setup. The one exception is local mode: a bare process bound to loopback lets this machine's browser and tools in as the owner until that owner sets a password. Tokens have scopes, are checked against their owner's role at each request, and never reach a backend. chatd trusts only requests that carry the forward key (X-Tandem-Forward).

Treat each of these as attacker-controlled:

  • every HTTP request that reaches the controller, chatd's front on 4180, or TandemNode: method, path, headers, body, chunked framing, WebSocket upgrades;
  • chat messages and their attachments, text files and images among them, and the PDFs and HTML pages the dashboard shows in a pane;
  • answers from backends, MCP servers, web_search results and pages that web_fetch reads;
  • the model's output. It picks the tool calls, and those run bash, write files and start servers inside the sandbox. A prompt injection in a fetched page can steer it;
  • whatever runs inside a sandbox: it owns /workspace and its home, and can swap a file for a symlink or a FIFO while chatd reads it;
  • config files the dashboard writes: backends, conductor config versions, the fleet's rules.

docs.title: Parts that matter most
docs.text:
In this order:

  1. Sessions and API tokens: the gate in proxy/accounts.py, the permission table in proxy/authz.py, tokens in proxy/tokens.py, local mode and the setup code in proxy/authlocal.py, and tandemapp/chat_forward.py and chatd/http.py. Any route without the permission it needs, a session that outlives its revocation, a token used beyond its scopes, models, expiry or its owner's role, a CSRF or cross-origin write, local mode reached through a proxy, a setup code that opens more than the setup, a forged forward key or X-Tandem-* header, or a credential that reaches a backend, a log or an answer.
  2. The sandbox boundary: a container setting that lets a chat reach the host, and egress bypasses in chatd/egress.py such as DNS rebinding, IPv4-mapped IPv6, redirects or CONNECT tricks that reach the LAN, the box or an engine's port. ops/sandbox/relay.py, which runs inside the container, is part of this.
  3. Path handling on the host for a chat's files: chatd/workspace.py (SandboxDir, O_NOFOLLOW walks), uploads (chatd/attach.py), snapshots, the files pane, the Open WebUI tool runner (chatd/owui.py). Traversal, symlink races and writes outside <data>/workspaces/<id>/ are in scope.
  4. Script from a sandbox page that runs on the dashboard's origin. Previews must stay in an opaque-origin iframe; the CSPs live in chatd/panes.py and chatd/preview.py, and the port proxy in chatd.
  5. HTTP handling we wrote: the chunked reader and keep-alive pool in proxy/http1.py, the byte forward and WebSocket splice in tandemapp/chat_forward.py, the egress proxy's request parsing. Request smuggling, header injection and unbounded reads count.
  6. Node trust (proxy.md, "Node trust"): a way to get a certificate pinned on a node or a controller without the code or SSH access, to beat the 5 tries of a pairing code, to reach a node's routes with an unpinned certificate or plain HTTP beyond loopback, or a password or key from SSH once that reaches a log, a file or an answer, or a password or pasted key from the Add Spark wizard (proxy.md, "Add Spark") that outlives its 30 minutes in the controller's memory, reaches the config database or the session's JSON; or an SSH login to the controller's own machine that pins anything in its agent's trust store.

These matter less and stay in scope: the dashboard's own XSS from server data, the conductor and memory routes, the metrics route.

Out of scope: bench/, the scripts under tools/ (measurement and evaluation; nothing serves them), docs/ and tests/.

docs.title: Where to test
docs.text:
Every CPU test is a standalone script: python tests/test_<name>.py, exit 0 is a pass. They need no GPU, no torch and no Docker; tests/test_sandbox_box.py needs Docker with the sandbox image.

area run it tests chat forward and chatd python -m chatd --port 8016 --data /tmp/chat; the key is in /tmp/chat/forward.key tests/test_chat_forward.py, tests/test_chatd.py, tests/test_chatd_agent.py sandbox and egress without Docker FakeBoxes in tests/chatd_util.py, RelayBoxes in tests/test_chatd_agent.py tests/test_chatd_sandbox_scope.py, tests/test_chatd_sandbox_lifecycle.py, tests/test_sandbox_relay_fd.py, tests/test_chatd_websearch.py workspace paths and uploads chatd as above tests/test_chatd_symlinks.py, tests/test_chatd_attach.py, tests/test_chatd_preview.py controller and relay python -m proxy --help; tests/fake_backend.py is a backend tests/test_proxy_relay.py, tests/test_proxy_http1_tls_fd.py, tests/test_proxy_model_card_auth.py dashboard cd dashboard && npm test dashboard/tests/*.test.ts

docs.title: Not in scope
docs.text:
• The quality or safety of model output.
  • Rate limits and resource use of the chat API for a client the deployment lets in.
  • A backend's own security: TandemApp passes requests on and records them.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Each entry is a symptom, what causes it, and what to do. The dashboard's Dev view shows the server log live. The engine's own entries (installing, the engine, memory notes) are in TandemEngine's troubleshooting.

docs.title: The dashboard
docs.text: Nobody can sign in, or an account lost its password. auth.md has the steps: a one-time code from an admin or tandem-app users reset-password NAME on the controller's machine, and tandem-app users setup-code while no owner exists.

docs.title: The Chat tab
docs.text:
The Chat tab is in beta (chat.md).

The Chat tab asks before every bash command. The chat runs in Ask mode. The pill in the composer's options row names the mode; pick Auto there, and calls that stay inside the chat's sandbox run without a prompt from the next call on. The default for new chats is at the top of the Tools settings page. A chat from before 0.8.2 has no mode of its own and runs in the default (chat.md).

Auto still asks. The call leaves the sandbox: web_fetch to a domain this chat has not fetched yet, an MCP tool its server does not mark read-only, an imported Open WebUI tool that imports a network or process module, or rm aimed at /, /workspace or a home directory. A tool set to “ask” in the tool settings asks in every mode, and a deny rule refuses in every mode, YOLO included.

“Always allow” does not stop the prompt. Before 0.8.2 it saved only the first word of a chained command, which never covered the whole command, so one chat saved cd 11 times. On 0.8.2 it saves a rule for every part and names them in the prompt. A command with $(...) or backticks still matches no rule and offers no “Always”; Auto runs it without asking when it stays in the sandbox.

docs.title: vLLM and SGLang behind the proxy
docs.text:
vLLM answers 400 to every request with tools. vLLM refuses tools without a tool parser. Start it with --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser <parser> (qwen3_coder for the Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.8 models). The memory writer sends the session's tools with tool_choice: "none", so it needs the parser too.

SGLang returns tool calls as text. Start it with --tool-call-parser <parser>. SGLang does not hold the model to tool_choice: "none"; the memory writer cuts any call it writes.

The SGLang card says the metrics page is off. SGLang answers /metrics with 404 unless it runs with --enable-metrics, and the plugin's hooks need it too.

Cached tokens read “not reported by this backend”. vLLM needs --enable-prompt-tokens-details, SGLang --enable-cache-report. A generic server fills prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens or not; the proxy never estimates.

Reasoning tokens are null, or the reasoning shows inside the answer. Start vLLM or SGLang with --reasoning-parser <parser> (qwen3 for Qwen).

The card says “L1 only”. No batch from the plugin for 60 s. In the engine's own Python, check that the plugin is installed, that TANDEM_COLLECT_URL names this proxy and this backend's id and is reachable from the engine's machine, and that TANDEM_COLLECT_TOKEN is the proxy's token. The engine's log has one line when the plugin fails to load; the engine starts either way. tandem-app launch ... --dry-run prints the variables it would set.

Rows say l2_join: approximate. The proxy could not tag the request (the Responses API, SGLang with n above 1) and matched it by time and token counts. A client that sends its own X-Request-Id (vLLM) or rid (SGLang) keeps it, and the join uses it.

docs.title: The proxy
docs.text:
401 or 403 from another device. Every request from another device needs an API token (Authorization: Bearer tdm-...); 401 names a token that is unknown, revoked or expired. 403 api_not_exposed means the protocol's switch is on this machine: set it to network under Settings, API. Make a token on the Access page or with tandem-app tokens create.

A save in the Backends view answers 422 and names a variable. A TANDEM_* variable sets that field, and the environment wins. Change the variable, or remove it and restart.

A request fails with key_unreadable. The master key that encrypted the backend's key does not answer: TANDEM_SECRETS_KEY changed, the keychain entry or secrets.key is gone, or the database was copied without its key. tandem-app secrets status says which source answers now. Type the backend's key in again.

TandemApp refuses to start and names a variable. An unknown TANDEM_* variable, an unknown backend id, or a value the schema refuses. tandem-app check --env-file app.env prints the same message without starting.

404 model_not_found. No rule, prefix or backend serves the id. When two backends serve one id, use <backend>/<model>, give one a public id, or add a routing rule.

The cost column is empty. The model has no price. Set one on the model's row, or with TANDEM_PRICE_<n>.

The System view shows no processes for a backend. The host setting is exporter, the process belongs to another user, or the proxy runs in docker without --pid=host. For a remote machine, run tandem-app hostcollect there with a token.

More entries for an install on Kubernetes are in install-kubernetes.md.

docs.title: Reference: commands
docs.text: The flags of every TandemApp command. tools/gen_reference.py reads them from the argument parsers, and python3 tools/gen_reference.py --check fails while a table is stale. tandem-app serve and python -m proxy take the same flags; tandem-app check, secrets and backends take them too and add their own action (install.md has every tandem-app subcommand). The engine's flags are in TandemEngine's reference.

docs.title: tandem-app serve and python -m proxy
docs.text: Flag Default What it does --config-db ~/.tandemllm/config.sqlite3 (TANDEM_CONFIG_DB) the config database (created when missing). --env-file none KEY=VALUE lines read before the start; the process environment wins. --host 127.0.0.1 (TANDEM_HOST) the address to bind. --port 8080 (TANDEM_PORT) the port to listen on. --usage-ledger ~/.tandemllm/ledger.sqlite3 (TANDEM_USAGE_LEDGER) the usage ledger (one row per request, no text); 'off' for none. --usage-retention-days 400 days the usage ledger keeps its rows (at least 400). --fleet-store beside (TANDEM_FLEET_STORE) the fleet's metric history, event log and alerts (SQLite); 'beside' puts fleet.sqlite3 next to the config database, 'off' keeps them in memory only. --fleet-retention-days 30 (TANDEM_FLEET_RETENTION_DAYS) days of 10-minute history, events and resolved alerts (at least 7). --dashboard-login none --dashboard-dir none default: dashboard/dist. --trust-loopback none --no-keychain off (a switch) do not ask the OS keychain for the master key. --conductor-config ~/.tandemllm/conductor (TANDEM_CONDUCTOR) the conductor's documents (profiles, router, packages) for the harness in front of the backends; 'off' relays every backend as does. --idle-timeout 60 (TANDEM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_S) seconds a client may take to send its request, or stay idle between requests, before the connection is closed (an answer has no timeout); 0 for none. --chat external (TANDEM_CHAT) who runs chatd, the Chat tab's service: off (nobody: Chat is off until an admin switches it on from the page; what a new install writes), external (TandemNode, an engine's launchers or a unit; the default when unset) or own (this ... One of: off, external, own. --conductor-defaults shipped what a new conductor directory starts with. One of: shipped, builtin. --verbose off (a switch) more log lines.

docs.title: tandem-app launch
docs.text: Flag Default What it does ENGINE the engine to start: vllm or sglang. --model required the model id or path the engine serves. --port none the engine's port. --host 127.0.0.1 the engine's bind address. --id none the backend id (default: the engine's name and port, e.g. vllm8100). --label none the backend's label in the dashboard. --config-db ~/.tandemllm/config.sqlite3 (TANDEM_CONFIG_DB) the proxy's config database the backend is registered in. --collect-url none (TANDEM_COLLECT_BASE) the proxy address the plugin posts to; default: this machine's proxy on its port. --engine-cmd none the engine's command instead of vllm serve / sglang serve. --python none the Python of the engine's environment, for the plugin check (default: the one behind the engine's command). --no-register off (a switch) do not create or update the backend. --dry-run off (a switch) print, start nothing.

docs.title: tandem-app hostcollect
docs.text: Flag Default What it does --host 127.0.0.1 the address to bind; beyond loopback it needs a token. --port 9108 the collector's port. --token-file none a file whose first line is the bearer token; else TANDEM_COLLECTOR_TOKEN. --watch none ports to report always, as id:port,id:port (a request may add more). --path [] a path whose filesystem to report (repeatable).

docs.title: Reference: HTTP
docs.text:
Every route, header and error TandemApp serves. The route, header and error tables are written by hand in tools/http_ref.py and checked against the code: a path the controller's handlers test, a header name or an error type the code uses that is missing here, or a row the code no longer has, fails python3 tools/gen_reference.py --check. The conductor's and the configuration routes come from their modules' route tables. The engine's own API is in TandemEngine's reference.

Every route but /health, the page and the sign-in needs an account's session or an API token; auth.md has the roles, the scopes and the recovery steps. The first table names the labels of the routes' who column.

docs.title: Who may call a controller route: the permission proxy/authz.py names, and the lowest role that holds it
docs.text: permission held by what it covers open anyone anyone who reaches the port: the page shell, /health's status, the sign-in and the first-run setup (which checks its own setup code) self viewer and up a signed-in person's own sessions, password, API tokens and usage users admin and up every account but the owners, every session, the audit session-address the session address a /s/<token>/ address: its token is the credential, for the library and Laya only collect:write a service identity a service identity only: a backend's collector or plugin (svc:collect:<id>) plugin-backend a service identity a service identity only: the plugin relay, in process read viewer and up every read of the page. For the fleet, the settings, the configuration and the conductor a write needs its kind's own permission too: settings:write, fleet:write or trust chat-engine a service identity a service identity only: chatd (svc:chatd) chat operator and up the Chat tab metrics:read viewer and up the Prometheus page inference viewer and up the data plane: the OpenAI and Messages API routes, the models, the library and Laya; an API token needs the protocol's scope (inference:openai, inference:anthropic)

docs.title: Who may call a route the extension serves inside an engine: the engine's own rule
docs.text: label who may call open anyone who reaches the port admin the admin rule: anyone while no admin password is set; with one, the admin token, a dashboard session, or a tool on the machine itself session only under a session address, /s/<token>/...

docs.title: The controller's routes (tandem-app)
docs.text: route permission what POST /v1/chat/completions inference Relayed to the backend the model id routes to (routing by model id); the answer's bytes go back unchanged. The same for /v1/completions, /v1/embeddings and /v1/responses. Body: the client's body. Answer: the backend's answer, with X-Tandem-Backend. POST /v1/completions inference As /v1/chat/completions. POST /v1/embeddings inference As /v1/chat/completions; not for deepseek backends. POST /v1/responses inference As /v1/chat/completions; openai backends only. GET /v1/models inference Every backend's models under their real ids, owned_by the backend. Answer: {object: list, data: [... with a tandem block]}. GET /v1/models/{id} inference One model's card. Answer: the card, or 404 model_not_found. GET / open Redirects to the dashboard. Answer: 302 to /dashboard/. GET /dashboard/ open The dashboard's static files. Answer: the page. GET /v1/dashboard/{view} read summary, usage, requests, system, live, logs, metrics, parallel and session, as on the engine; the engine-only panels answer 404. Answer: as on the engine. POST /v1/dashboard/session open As on the engine. Body: {token}. Answer: the session. * /v1/config/* read The Backends and Setup screens (the configuration routes). GET /v1/fleet/* read TandemApp's fleet (the fleet): nodes, links, topology, deployments, per-node metrics, memory, logs, events, alerts, rules and a page's window layout, as app/contracts/fleet-v1 says. Answer: the contract's JSON. * /v1/fleet/* read The fleet's writes: PATCH /v1/fleet/nodes/{id} (alias, colour, icon, tags), PUT /v1/fleet/layouts/{page}, POST /v1/fleet/alerts/{id}/ack. Body: the contract's body. Answer: the node, the layout as saved, or the alert. POST /v1/collect/{backend} collect:write A plugin's batch (as on the engine). GET /metrics metrics:read The proxy's own Prometheus families. Answer: Prometheus text format. GET /health open The proxy's health, for a container's check; the full body for the admin or the machine. Also /healthz and /v1/health. Answer: {status}. * /v1/conductor/* read The conductor in front of the backends, with --conductor-config; the engine-only screens answer 404. GET /v1/library inference The package library, as on the engine, also under /v1/library/*. GET /v1/laya inference Laya, when the decider role names an endpoint. POST /v1/laya/ask inference As on the engine, relayed to the decider role's endpoint. POST /v1/messages inference The Messages API: translated to a chat completion and run through the pipeline, or passed through untouched when every backend of the model's route is of kind anthropic (docs/proxy.md). Body: the Messages API's body, the key as x-api-key or a bearer. Answer: the Messages API's answer or event stream, with request-id. POST /v1/messages/count_tokens inference The prompt's exact token count from a backend that can count it; any other answers 404 not_found_error. Answer: {input_tokens}. POST /v1/cache/peek inference With a deployment's model: relayed to the member that holds the conversation; the same for /v1/cache/prewarm and /v1/cache/release. Without the model: 400 model_required. Body: {model, session?, ...}. Answer: the member's answer, with X-Tandem-Node and X-Tandem-Deployment. POST /v1/cache/prewarm inference As /v1/cache/peek. POST /v1/cache/release inference As /v1/cache/peek. GET\|POST\|DELETE /v1/auth/session open Who this request is (account, role, permissions, CSRF token, provider, setup_required, local_mode); POST signs in, DELETE signs out (docs/auth.md). Body: POST: {username, password}. Answer: the session; the cookie on a sign-in. POST /v1/auth/setup open The first owner, with the one-time setup code; 404 once an owner exists. Body: {code, username, password}. Answer: the session. PUT /v1/auth/password self A signed-in person's own password. Body: {current, password}. GET\|DELETE /v1/auth/sessions self The live sessions (?user= another's, with the users permission); DELETE ends them, DELETE .../{id} one. GET\|POST\|PATCH\|DELETE /v1/auth/tokens self API tokens (?all=1 every account's): POST makes one, PATCH /{id} changes one, DELETE /{id} revokes, POST /{id}/rotate, GET /{id}/usage. Answer: a new token's secret once. GET\|POST\|PATCH\|DELETE /v1/auth/users users The accounts: POST makes one, PATCH /{id} changes one, DELETE /{id} removes one, POST /{id}/reset a one-time code. GET /v1/auth/audit users Sign-ins, sessions, accounts, tokens and the auth settings, as audit rows. GET /v1/auth/usage self What an account used (?user= another's, with the users permission). GET /v1/chat-app/capabilities read What the Chat tab can do here: whether chatd answers, the sandbox, the session. * /v1/chat-app/* chat The Chat tab: relayed to chatd behind the controller (off, own or external; docs/chat.md). Answer: chatd's answer. GET\|POST /s/{token}/v1/library/* session-address The library and Laya under a session address, the address the notes give the model, journaled to that session. * /v1/settings/* read The settings interface over every store: scopes, change sets, versions and restore, the audit (docs/settings.md). Reads need the read permission, writes the scope's own. Body: the contract's body. Answer: the contract's JSON. GET /plugin-panels/{id}/{panel}/ read A running plugin's panel: its HTML and the files beside it, served sandboxed for the page's frame (docs/plugins.md). Answer: the panel's files. * /plugin-backends/{id}/{name} plugin-backend A plugin's backend, the URL of its row in the backends store; the gateway routes a model there. From this machine only (403 forbidden otherwise). Body: the relayed request. Answer: the plugin's answer.

docs.title: The host collector beside the controller
docs.text: server route answer tandem-app hostcollect GET /host?watch= the machine's sample as JSON (the bearer token when --token is set) tandem-app hostcollect GET /metrics the same sample in the Prometheus text format tandem-app hostcollect GET /health {status: ok}, no token

docs.title: The routes the extension serves inside an engine
docs.text: route who what * /v1/conductor/* admin The conductor's documents, journal, sessions and memory (the conductor's routes). Reads follow the dashboard rule, writes and every memory route the admin rule. On a headless engine, or one without --conductor-config, 404. GET /v1/laya open What the Laya route takes and answers, its limits, and whether it is on. Answer: a description of the route. POST /v1/laya/ask open A typed answer from Laya on one text or many, for the model's own scripts; rate-limited. Body: {question, choices \| scale \| neither, text \| texts, threshold?, model?, deadline_ms?}. Answer: {label, p, sure, probs, model, ms, ...}, or {answers: [...]} for texts. POST /v1/laya/drive/end open Ends a playtest driver session and writes its journal row. Body: the session's summary. Answer: the row. GET /v1/laya/kit/{file} open A file of the playtest kit the model copies into a project. Answer: the file. OPTIONS /v1/laya/* open A browser's CORS preflight for the Laya routes. Every other path answers OPTIONS with 501. Answer: 204 with the CORS headers. GET /v1/library open The package library: every enabled skill's name, description and classes. Answer: the list and the two routes below. GET /v1/library/search?q=&k=&class= open BM25 search over the skills, best first (k from 1 to 20, default 5). Answer: [{name, description, score}]. GET /v1/library/{name} open One skill's text and its reference. Answer: {name, description, classes, body, reference}. GET /s/{token}/v1/memory session The memory index this session sees. The /s/{token}/ prefix also serves the library and Laya routes, filed to the session. Answer: the notes' index lines. GET /s/{token}/v1/memory/search?q=&k= session Memory notes that match, best first (k from 1 to 10). Answer: [{id, kind, scope, status, title, score}]. GET /s/{token}/v1/memory/{id} session One note. Answer: {id, title, kind, scope, status, body, ...}. POST /s/{token}/v1/memory session Writes, changes or archives a note, with the fields of the hidden memory block. Body: {op, scope, kind, title, tags, body, id, reason}. Answer: {op, id, title, ...}, or 422 with the reason as the type.

note?}: the three-way switch GET /v1/conductor/roles the document, health, and what each role's tokenizer hash allows it to share POST /v1/conductor/roles/{role}/test one question, its latency and answer GET /v1/conductor/packages/scan skills found in skill_dirs on the box GET /v1/conductor/packages/catalog every package: category, tokens on the engine's tokenizer, limit, classes, library docs.text: Method Path What GET /v1/config everything the screens show, in one answer POST /v1/config/test {kind?, url, key?}: test a backend not saved; the answer says reason (key_rejected, unreachable, not_openai) when it fails POST /v1/config/backends {url, id?, kind?, key?,...}: add. kind defaults to generic (any OpenAI-compatible server), id to a free one made from the label or the URL's host. GET /v1/config/presets the providers the page offers (proxy/presets.py) GET /v1/config/backends/{id} one, with its models PATCH /v1/config/backends/{id} change fields (key: null removes the key) DELETE /v1/config/backends/{id} POST /v1/config/backends/{id}/test test the saved backend, refresh its models PUT /v1/config/backends/{id}/models/{model} public id, enabled, price, max_output (null clears), fallback, features (creates a manual model) DELETE /v1/config/backends/{id}/models/{model} PUT /v1/config/rules {rules: [{id?, pattern, backend, enabled}]} GET /v1/config/prices/seed the public list prices shipped with this release, applied only by a click GET /v1/config/audit the last 50 changes (field names only)

docs.title: Every header TandemApp reads or writes
docs.text: header direction, where meaning x-api-key in, controller a Messages API client's credential, as an API token or a backend key would be sent as a bearer; removed from the request once checked X-Tandem-Auth out, controller accounts on /health: the controller runs the accounts sign-in, so a front proxy asks it X-Tandem-CSRF in, controller a cookie request that writes carries the session's token (GET /v1/auth/session returns it); without it 403 X-Tandem-Dropped out, controller the client's fields a translated request went without (a Messages API field the chat shape has no place for, thinking the stash evicted) X-Tandem-Hook both, controller to a webhook: the hook's id; on an answer a guard refused: the hook that refused it X-Tandem-Delivery out, controller to a webhook: the call's id, also the body's id, which the signature covers X-Tandem-Timestamp out, controller to a webhook: unix seconds, inside the signed text X-Tandem-Signature out, controller to a webhook: v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256(secret, timestamp.body)>, one v1= per secret while a secret rotates (docs/hooks.md) X-Tandem-* out, controller every X-Tandem- answer header, and the backend's anthropic-ratelimit-* headers, also reach a Messages API client X-Tandem both, both raw, shadow or on: lowers the conductor's mode for one request; the response says which mode ran X-Tandem-Profile both, both picks a conductor profile; the response names the profile that ran; an unknown name is a 400 X-Tandem-Memory in, engine off: no memory note is read or written; read: reads only, a block the model writes is hidden and dropped X-Tandem-User in, engine a proxy's user name for the memory notes, honoured from loopback or QWEN38_MEMORY_PROXIES X-Tandem-Relay-Id in, engine a proxy's id for a relayed request, for the live counts; a relayed request without X-Tandem-User touches no memory X-Tandem-Parent in, engine the request a call of TandemLLM to itself serves; the row becomes client kind internal X-Tandem-Forward out, engine to chatd on a /v1/chat-app request: the forward key, the only proof chatd accepts X-Tandem-Principal out, engine to chatd: who the request is for (owner) X-Tandem-Password-Set out, engine to chatd: 1 when an admin password is set X-Tandem-Signed-In out, engine to chatd: 1 when the request passed the dashboard's rule X-Tandem-Backend out, proxy the id of the backend that answered a relayed request X-Tandem-Deployment out, proxy the deployment that answered a request the gateway routed to one of its members X-Tandem-Node out, proxy the alias of the node whose engine answered a request the gateway routed X-Tandem-Pin in, proxy a node's id or alias: the request goes to that member of the deployment and to no other (the Playground's A/B of a deployment's members) X-Tandem-Gateway out, proxy tandem-app on the controller's /v1/models answers, so a page behind a reverse proxy knows whether its /v1 reaches the controller or an engine X-Tandem-Bundle out, both on the page's files: the bundle's tag, or none while no bundle is built and the placeholder answers X-Tandem-Copy-Token in, proxy TandemNode: the token of one weights copy between two nodes; a file sent without it is refused X-Tandem-Cost in, proxy 1 on a streamed relayed request: one SSE comment before data: [DONE] carries the request's cost (: tandem-cost {"cost_micros": N, "backend": id}); without it the stream is the backend's x-session-id in, both opencode's session id: the router's session and the caches' session key X-Conversation-Id in, both a conversation id for clients that send no session field; read after the body's own ids X-OpenWebUI-Chat-Id in, both Open WebUI's chat id (a connection header with {{CHAT_ID}}): the router's session for that chat X-Request-Id both, proxy sent to a vllm backend as px-<hex>, which the plugin reports back for the join; a client's own id is kept X-QSE-Client in, engine dashboard marks the dashboard's own requests (client kind dashboard) X-Real-IP in, both set by a reverse proxy; a request that carries it is never trusted as local; the sign-in's rate limit counts per address X-Forwarded-For in, both as X-Real-IP: a request that carries it is never trusted as local X-Forwarded-Proto in, both https makes the session cookie Secure, and the notes' {tandem_url} https X-Forwarded-Host in, engine the host the notes' {tandem_url} names, unless QWEN38_TANDEM_URL sets it X-Accel-Buffering out, both no, on every stream, so nginx sends each event at once X-Content-Type-Options out, both nosniff on the dashboard's static files x-ratelimit-* out, proxy a cloud backend's rate-limit headers, passed on to the client OpenAI-Beta both, proxy a client's OpenAI-Beta header, passed on to an openai backend Authorization in, both Bearer: an API token (tdm-...), a service identity's token (a collector, chatd) or a management token for scripts, by route (docs/auth.md); the engine's OpenAI routes ignore it and file the request under a hash of it User-Agent in, both the client kind in the ledger: open-webui, opencode, openai-sdk, curl, other (a Hermes-shaped body: hermes) Last-Event-ID in, both resumes the log stream after that line Retry-After out, both with a 503 (queue full, memory gate, draining, a full backend), a 429, or a decision model that is loading WWW-Authenticate out, both Bearer, with a 401 Set-Cookie out, both qse_dash, the dashboard session: HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Secure behind https Access-Control-Allow-Origin out, engine * on the library and Laya routes, so a page the model builds can call them; with Access-Control-Allow-Methods, -Headers and -Max-Age on the preflight Access-Control-Allow-Methods out, engine on the Laya preflight Access-Control-Allow-Headers out, engine on the Laya preflight Access-Control-Max-Age out, engine on the Laya preflight

docs.title: The errors explained
docs.text: status error.type or code when 400 invalid_request_error a request TandemApp will not relay as asked: error.param names the field 400 bad_request a dashboard, fleet or conductor query or body that does not parse (a level, a range, a number, a body that is not an object) 400 model_required a cache route through the gateway without the model that names the deployment 400 context_length_exceeded a prompt and max_tokens that no member of the deployment has the window for 401 unauthorized a route that needs a credential, without a session or an API token, or with one that is unknown, revoked or expired; a wrong collect token; wrong_credentials: a sign-in whose name or password is wrong 401 invalid_api_key the data plane (OpenAI shape): no API token, a token it does not know, or two credentials that name different tokens (code invalid_api_key) 403 forbidden a memory route outside a known session address; a cross-site write; a weights copy with another token 403 wrong_password PUT /v1/auth/password whose current password is not right 404 not_found no such route, or a route whose part is off on this server (the conductor, the backends, the fleet) 404 unsupported_route the proxy: a route the backend's kind does not serve, such as embeddings on deepseek (code unsupported_route) 404 model_not_found a model id no backend serves, or one two backends serve (the message names the prefixed forms) (code model_not_found) 405 method_not_allowed the sign-in routes, the accounts or the Setup Guide's relay with a method they do not take 409 busy an Add Spark session or an install that already runs; a chatd job that runs on TandemNode 409 closed, stale a package proposal already closed, or whose base text changed since 409 conflict an Add Spark session in another state, a device picked twice, more devices than one add takes 409 not_a_member X-Tandem-Pin names a node that is not a member of the deployment 413 too_large a request body over the limit (a fleet request's body over 4 MiB) 422 invalid_request_error, invalid_report a value the schema refuses: a config field (error.field), a field an environment variable locks (error.variable), a Laya, library or memory call's fields, an eval report 422 schema, secret, cap, user, unknown_id, unknown_package, rule_from_tool, no_session, no_user, refused_root, no_proposals, propose a memory note or a package proposal refused, with the reason as the type: a field (schema), a secret, a cap, an unknown note or package 429 with Retry-After too_many a fifth log or live stream at once; a sixth failed sign-in in a minute; too many wrong passwords or pairing attempts 429 with Retry-After rate_limited the library, Laya or memory routes past their calls a minute 500 internal_error, error a bug, or a fleet job that failed on an exception: the message is the exception's 502 connect_error, upstream_error, key_unreadable the proxy could not reach the backend or read its stored key, after its retries 502 unreachable Add Spark: a paired device whose agent does not answer, or answers with an error 200 upstream_closed, upstream_error a stream that already began: the backend failed or closed early; the client gets an error event, then [DONE] 503 with Retry-After server_busy a backend or a deployment that cannot take the request now; error.code says why (the codes below) 503 with Retry-After max_inflight every backend for the model is at the max_inflight you set (Retry-After: 1) 503 with Retry-After deployment_stopped a request for a deployment that is stopped, or a Split without a plan 503 with Retry-After no_member, member_not_serving a deployment with no member that takes requests now, or the pinned member does not 503 with Retry-After node_draining a member whose node is drained for maintenance 503 with Retry-After not_loaded a Laya call while the engine has handed over no decision model 504 upstream_timeout, timeout a backend that sent no first byte in time; a Laya call past its deadline

docs.title: Reference: metrics and the usage ledger
Metrics
docs.text: The controller's /metrics carries the proxy's families and the mapped engine families as qse_backend_*; an engine in chat mode carries the conductor's, the families the engine contract marks "owner": "ext". The collector's /metrics carries tandem_host_*. tools/gen_reference.py reads them from the metric registrations.

docs.title: Prometheus families TandemApp registers: the conductor's inside an engine, the proxy's and the collector's
docs.text: Metric Type, labels What it counts qse_conductor_decisions_total counter, task, tier, mode, decision conductor decisions, passes included: the monitor's tasks and the router's class (task route) qse_conductor_actions_total counter, task, action decisions the conductor executed, by task and action qse_conductor_hidden_tokens_total counter tokens the model saw that the client did not send or receive (hidden closes, hidden turns, reminders, router notes new and replayed) qse_conductor_gave_up_total counter turns the conductor ended with its GIVE_UP sentence qse_conductor_tier1_seconds histogram one tier 1 question (a classifier stage: the decider or Qwen), answered or not qse_conductor_tier1_failures_total counter, reason tier 1 questions without a usable answer, by reason qse_conductor_package_kept_out_total counter, why, mode packages the router kept out of a turn because an offered tool delivers their result, by why and by mode (act, shadow) qse_conductor_reasoning_tokens_cut_total counter reasoning tokens written before a hidden close cut the block (the size of the blocks the conductor closed) qse_proxy_requests_total counter, backend, kind, finish_reason requests relayed to a backend, by its id, its kind and the finish reason qse_proxy_tokens_total counter, backend, type tokens a backend reported in usage, by type (prompt, cached, completion, reasoning) qse_proxy_cost_micros_total counter, backend cost at the model's price, micro-dollars qse_upstream_retries_total counter, backend, reason tries again before any byte reached the client, by backend and reason (429, 502, 503, connect) qse_proxy_overhead_ms histogram the proxy's own time per request: arrival to the upstream send, plus the first frame's delay through the proxy qse_proxy_ttft_seconds histogram arrival at the proxy to the first token frame (the network and the backend's queue inside) qse_backend_up gauge, backend 1 when the backend's last health check passed qse_backend_inflight gauge, backend requests relayed to the backend now qse_backend_scrape_age_seconds gauge, backend seconds since the backend's own /metrics page was last read (vLLM, SGLang) qse_backend_plugin_age_seconds gauge, backend seconds since the plugin inside the backend's engine last posted (vLLM, SGLang with tandemllm-*-plugin) qse_backend_plugin_joins gauge, backend, join requests whose ledger row got the engine's own numbers, by how the plugin's item was matched (exact, approximate) or why it was not (unmatched, untagged)

docs.title: The usage ledger
docs.text: The controller keeps one SQLite row per request it relays, in the same schema as the engine's ledger, and the conductor's journal in the same file.

docs.title: Reference: variables and knobs
docs.text: The proxy, the collector and the plugins read TANDEM_* variables. TandemApp's code reads some of the engine's QSE_* variables too, where it starts chatd, runs TandemNode or reads the engine's files. Inside an engine the conductor reads the QWEN38_* knobs the engine contract names (contracts/engine-ext-v1/knobs.json), with the defaults of tandemapp/knobs.py. tools/gen_reference.py builds every table here from the code. The old sign-in's variables, which the first start imports once, are in auth.md.
